articleTitle: Knowledge-Based Recommendations and Clustering for Determining Agricultural Crops
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Determining the type of crop suitable for the land is crucial to increasing agricultural productivity and sustainability. This study proposes a combined approach between a recommendation system and knowledge-based clustering to assist the decision-making process in selecting optimal crops. The recommendation system uses a knowledge base in the form of a collection of data and relationships between land characteristics and crop needs. In addition, the clustering method groups land based on similarities in agro-climate and soil parameters, such as potential of hydrogen or power of hydrogen (pH), rainfall, temperature, and nutrient content. The clustering results are used to develop more specific and contextual crop recommendation strategies for each land group. This approach improves the accuracy of crop recommendations and provides flexibility in its application in various regions with diverse environmental conditions. System evaluation using agricultural data shows combining clustering and knowledge-based recommendations can provide more relevant results than conventional methods. This study found that four clusters had optimal results even though the data visualization overlapped, and the best accuracy results were obtained for the Random Forest model.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction with Information Extraction for Embedding Feature in Twitter Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Sentiment analysis on social media like Twitter is an NLP process that analyzes sentiment based on unstructured text information. NLP incorporates word-level Information Extraction (IE) as an extra feature and as a regular feature. Previous sentiment analysis always removed unnecessary words like stop-words and the embedding process was always word by word. Textual removal cannot be performed conventionally because IE requires every word and symbol inside of text for optimal performance. research before rarely use IE inside the embedding. This research proposes using IE as a feature extraction method for embedding to represent text numerically. This research also compares the proposed feature extraction method with base-line feature extraction methods commonly used in previous studies. Experiments for this research were conducted on the sentiment140 dataset and were evaluated with accuracy, precision, recall and f1 Score. Based on proposed methodology, this research shows us that using IE for feature extraction with stop-word variation connected gives best evaluation performance on a logistic model with F1-score 0.697.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Convolutional Neural Network-Based Transfer Learning Models in Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Facial recognition is an important aspect of vision that is popular in the security, surveillance, and biometric fields because it does not require any physical contact. However, problems such as occlusion, illumination, and differences in pose are some of the issuses that make it a difficult area to focus on. In this study, the effectiveness of five Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) using transfer learning are evaluated, namely, MobileNetV1, MobileNetV2, VGG16, ResNet50, and InceptionV3 on Pins Face Recognition dataset. The simulations were carried out in the Google Colab environment using Python due to its GPU acceleration which enabled the models to train faster. The MobileNet model was able to achieve an accuracy of 59.468%, which was the highest among the models analyzed and demonstrates its viability in analyzing the dataset provided. On the other hand, ResNet50 and InceptionV3 performed suboptimally at accuracy of 9.412% and 44.324% respectively. The MobileNet models’ strength lies in its focus to work in unbalanced datasets without compromising performance on rigorous conditions, which makes it standout for face recognition tasks. These observations have important implications regarding the design and deployment of CNN-based models and structures as well as paving the way for further studies in the future.

articleTitle: Relative Uplift in Online Experimentation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The culture of experimentation, implemented by successful big data companies, allows for data-driven decision-making, the creation of valuable products and services, attracting new and retaining existing clients, and increasing profits. One of the research challenges in online experimentation is obtaining advanced results for ratio metrics, which are highly popular in e-commerce. Relative improvement, or relative uplift, plays a pivotal role in online randomized experiments and quantifies the performance difference between two user groups evaluating the impact of a specific change. Decision-makers rely on relative uplift to evaluate the effectiveness of changes and develop optimization strategies. In this research paper, novel analytical solutions for relative uplift are introduced. Bayesian approach is proposed to estimate parameters for the relative uplift distribution during continuous monitoring of user data. The mixture sequential probability ratio test is recommended to evaluate hypotheses based on sequentially received user data during online randomized experiments. Sequential hypothesis testing is an effective tool for enhancing user experience, perfecting user interface design, and boosting user click rates.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Performance of Audio Codecs for Electronic Know Your Customer in Bandwidth-Constrained Networks Using NS-3
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In the Electronic Know Your Customer (eKYC) process, audio and video transmission plays a crucial role in the identity verification procedure. However, bandwidth limitations pose a significant challenge to transmission quality, so it is necessary to select the right audio codec so that eKYC can run efficiently and reliably. Our research aims to evaluate the performance that includes throughput, delay, jitter, and packet loss on three audio codecs, namely Advanced Audio Encoding (AAC), OGG Vorbis, and Opus. The evaluation was carried out through simulation using NS-3 network simulator tools. Based on the test results, the bandwidth requirements that can be used at high bitrates to get good audio transmission quality, especially in the eKYC process, are in the range above 512 Kbps where the bandwidth is able to maintain the quality of the transmitted audio. Meanwhile, low to medium bitrates can use a minimum bandwidth of 256 kbps. However, bandwidth usage in eKYC applications can be reduced by adjusting the bitrate parameters and also the duration of the audio transmitted to be used at very limited bandwidth.

articleTitle: The Combination of the Leiden Algorithm and Graph Coloring for Influencers Detection in Large Scale Social Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The role of influencers, especially on social media platforms, has grown significantly. A commonly used feature among business professionals today is follower grouping. However, this feature is limited to identifying influencers based solely on mutual followership, underscoring the need for a more sophisticated approach to influencer detection.This study proposes a new method for influencer detection that integrates the Leiden Coloring Algorithm and Matrix Centrality. This approach leverages network analysis to identify patterns and relationships in large-scale datasets. First, the Leiden Coloring Algorithm partitions the network into various communities, which are considered potential influencer groups. Furthermore, Eigenvector and Degree Centrality augment this process by identifying nodes with high connectivity, representing potential influencers.The proposed method is validated using crawled data from the Twitter (X) social media platform with the keyword "GarudaIndonesia." The results of the Leiden Coloring Algorithm recommend 10 accounts as influencers. Based on Eigenvector Centrality and Degree Centrality for a dataset of 1,000 rows, it is observed that the first and second ranks consistently identify the same influencers, namely IndonesiaGaruda and GarudaCares. However, the third to tenth ranks suggest different influencers. For a dataset of 5,000 rows, both methods again identify IndonesiaGaruda as the top-ranked influencer, while the second to tenth ranks differ between the two methods.The modularity value for the first test scenario is 0.9396, while for the second test scenario, it is 0.9381. The processing time for the first test scenario is 29.5493 seconds, compared to 434.1838 seconds for the second test scenario. Additionally, the number of communities identified by the Leiden Coloring Algorithm increases with dataset size, with 505 communities for the first test scenario and 1,969 communities for the second. This demonstrates that larger datasets result in a higher number of communities identified by the Leiden Coloring Algorithm.

articleTitle: Side Effect Prediction by Using Bees Algorithm-Support Vector Machine: Case Study Reproductive System and Breast Disorders
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The development of pharmaceuticals has significantly improved human quality of life and life expectancy. However, medicines can also cause potentially adverse side effects. Studies have shown that most drugs have the potential to produce side effects. Traditionally, evaluating drug side effects involves testing on experimental animals, but this approach has limitations in generalizing the results to humans. As a result, in silico methods have emerged as a promising alternative for predicting drug side effects without animal testing. While machine learning has shown potential in predicting drug side effects, the importance of feature selection has often been overlooked. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the Bees Algorithm in feature selection and improve the performance of drug side effect prediction through hyperparameter tuning on a Support Vector Machine (SVM) model optimized with the Bees Algorithm. The best model, using the RBF kernel, achieved an accuracy of 0.6578 and an F1-score of 0.6561. The results are expected to enhance the understanding and management of drug side effects more efficiently.

articleTitle: Circular Arc Based Path Smoothing for Precise Forklift Navigation and Orientation Alignment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Autonomous forklifts in warehousing operations require precise path planning, especially for pallet handling tasks where the orientation of the final vehicle must be aligned with the pallet position. This paper presents an enhanced path planning approach that addresses both kinematic constraints and orientation requirements through a three-stage solution. First, a Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithm generates a global optimal path in a complex warehousing environment, ensuring optimal route from start to goal position. Second, an circular arc-based smoothing technique is applied to corners to ensure a continuous curvature path that satisfies the forklift turning radius. Finally, a novel 4-arc-based method is introduced to specifically handle the initial and final orientation constraints, ensuring precise maneuvers alignment with both pickup and placement orientations. This comprehensive approach enables smooth transitions throughout the entire path while guaranteeing precise orientation during forklift operations, effectively bridging the gap between theoretical path planning and practical warehousing automation requirements.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Louvain and Leiden Coloring Algorithms in Influencer Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In today's digital era, the influence of social media influencers has grown significantly. A commonly used feature by business professionals today is follower grouping. However, this feature is limited to identifying influencers based solely on mutual followership, highlighting the need for a more sophisticated approach to influencer detection. This study proposes a novel method for influencer detection that integrates the Leiden coloring algorithm and Degree centrality. This approach leverages network analysis to identify patterns and relationships within large-scale datasets. First, the Leiden coloring algorithm is employed to partition the network into distinct communities, identifying potential influencer clusters. Subsequently, Degree centrality is utilized to identify nodes within these communities exhibiting high connectivity, indicating individuals with significant influence. The proposed method was validated using data crawled from Twitter (X) social media, employing the keyword "GarudaIndonesia." The data was collected using Tweet-Harvest between January 1, 2020, and October 16, 2024, resulting in a dataset of 22,623 rows. The proposed method was compared to the Louvain coloring method, demonstrating an increase in the modularity value of the Leiden coloring algorithm by 0.0195, a reduction in processing time by 13.93 seconds, and a decrease in the number of communities by 649.

articleTitle: Improving Real-Time Attendance System Based On Yolo and Facenet Using Super Resolution Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: A real-time attendance system that uses the face recognition model can reduce workload rather than manual attendance. One of the problems of the real-time attendance system with face recognition is the low quality of face images detected from a long distance. The solution To overcome this problem is by combining several deep learning models like YOLOv11, super-resolution (SR) models that use GAN architecture like ESRGAN, Real-ESRGAN, and GFPGAN, Facenet is trained with Casia-WebFace and VGG-Face2 datasets. All datasets and detected faces are aligned with Mediapipe. Face recognition is done by measuring the distance between embeddings using cosine similarity. The dataset contains Indonesian faces with various poses, expressions, and illuminations. The dataset is processed again to become two datasets, one resized to 64x64 pixels and one not resized. Tests were carried out using video recordings containing the activities of students who entered the classroom simultaneously and were taken using a webcam remotely. The results show that Facenet trained with VGG-Face2 is very suitable for the Indonesian dataset. GFPGAN can produce more realistic facial images than other SR models. The resized dataset can improve the quality of face recognition because the resized dataset is suitable for detected faces that have some missing facial information. YOLOv11m-Face and YOLOv11n-Face can improve the quality of face recognition than combination of YOLOv11s-Face and GFPGAN there are unrecognized faces. The test results recommended a combination of models (YOLOv11m-Face or YOLOv11n-Face), GFPGAN, Facenet is trained with VGG-Face2 dataset, and resized dataset.

articleTitle: Design Of A ‘ Drive Wave ‘ System based on Communications System Remote Real-time Running Text and Speech to Text Converter using Light Emitting Diode (LED) Display
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Drive Wave is a device that can help drivers communicate with other road users by displaying familiar words and icons as well as a speech to text feature that can make it easier for drivers to communicate with other road users. in this work, a system design prototype consisting of two devices, namely Remote and LED message board. The most spoken words used and icons displayed on the LED message board are controlled wireless using a Remote using the ESP-NOW protocol and Bluetooth Low Energy (Bluetooth LE). The two ways of he LED message board controlled by the remote are manual and automatic speech to text converter system controlled the LED message board displayed. the manual way, the user pressed the button to choice the word to be displayed. in the automatic voiced control, the LED displayed the word uttered by the user. the automatic voiced controlled applied Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCC) as feature extraction techniques and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) method for word identification methods. The results showed that the automatic voice controlled 99.78% and 100% for training and validating accuracy, respectively. the real testing result showed that 24 times testing which have 100% accuracy.

articleTitle: Intelligent CCTV-based Attendance System Leveranging Haar Cascade Classifier for Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study aims to develop and implement a smart attendance system that automatically recognizes employee faces through CCTV cameras using the Haar Cascade Classifier method to enhance attendance efficiency and accuracy. The research encompasses a comprehensive literature review, data collection, system development, and data analysis. The Haar Cascade Classifier, known for its effectiveness in object detection, particularly in facial recognition, was employed as the core method. Testing was conducted under various conditions, yielding the following results: with 50 face data samples, the system achieved 100% accuracy under bright lighting at close distances and at distances greater than 100 cm. It also achieved 98% accuracy under dim lighting at close distances and at distances greater than 100 cm. These results demonstrate the Haar Cascade Classifier's robustness to varying lighting conditions and distances, confirming its reliability for real-world applications. The system's ability to consistently achieve accuracy rates above 90% highlights its potential as an effective tool for enhancing security and attendance tracking in organizational environments. Furthermore, these findings suggest opportunities for future development, including integration with other biometric systems, to further improve efficiency and security.

articleTitle: An Exploration of Convolutional Neural Network For Breast Cancer Classification Using METABRIC RNA Mutation Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Research and studies have consistently demonstrated that classifying breast cancer subtypes with RNA Sequencing data has the potential to yield more crucial information for advancing research. However, the algorithms developed for achieving high accuracy is still continue to face obstacles. In response to these challenges, this research proposed approach using both modified deep learning and machine learning. Specifically, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model was implemented and compared to Support Vector Machine (SVM) leveraging RNA Mutation (METABRIC) Data, by varying the number of epochs in intervals of 20 until 100 and batch size in the intervals of 8 until 64 for Convolutional Neural Network, also the kernels, random state, and C parameters for Support Vector Machine. The findings of this research have achieved an outstanding overall accuracy of 99.21%. The accuracy not only reflects the robustness of the proposed method architecture but also exceeded the performance of the comparison model by 11.03% and 1.05%.

articleTitle: A Model of Sentiment Analysis on Gojek Application Review using Word Vector Representation and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Gojek is the most popular online transportation application in Indonesia and several countries in Southeast Asia. The Gojek application is highly beneficial for handling transportation issues in regions such as Jakarta, Yogyakarta, Surabaya and others. Gojek users often share their experiences and opinions on social media and user review platforms. In this research, we aim to conduct sentiment analysis on customer responses to Gojek's transportation services using data collected from Twitter. Our model adopts word embedding to transform text into vector dimensions using Word2Vec and the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) algorithm as the classification engine. The dataset consists of three classes: positive, negative, and neutral. A total of 2,535 datasets were collected from Twitter. The hybridization of Word2Vec and LSTM achieved significant performance improvements in the classification task, reaching accuracies of 75.2% and 91.75%. We attribute the success of our model to the effectiveness of Word2Vec in enhancing word vector representations and the robust classification capabilities of LSTM. However, our model also faced challenges, such as misclassification of some reviews. To further enhance the model, we plan to explore other word vector models, such as GloVe and FastText, in future research.

articleTitle: Evaluating Lifestyle Factors Contributing to Diabetes Using K-Means Clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Diabetes is a rapidly growing global health concern, affecting millions of individuals and placing a significant burden on healthcare systems. Understanding the lifestyle factors contributing to diabetes is essential for effective prevention and management. This study evaluates lifestyle factors contributing to diabetes using K-means clustering based on data collected from Puskesmas Jayanti. By applying K-means clustering, we identified distinct lifestyle patterns associated with an increased risk of diabetes. The analysis revealed critical factors such as smoking, physical inactivity, high sugar intake, frequent consumption of junk food, and low dietary fibre intake as significant contributors to diabetes risk. The clustering results provided actionable insights for targeted interventions for diabetes. Consequently, we recommend quitting smoking, regular exercise, reducing sugar consumption, avoiding junk food, and increasing dietary fibre intake as effective strategies to mitigate the risk of diabetes. This study underscores the importance of data-driven approaches in understanding and addressing lifestyle-related health issues.

articleTitle: Bagworm Pest Detection in Oil Palm Plantations using Deep Learning Based on Aerial Imagery Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The rapid detection and management of bagworm pests in oil palm plantations are critical for maintaining crop health and productivity. Manual detection of bagworm pests is time-consuming and labor-intensive by observing defoliating of oil palm crop. This research aims to develop a machine learning model capable of accurately detecting and classifying infested, healthy, and unhealthy palm oil trees using the YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once) algorithm based on deep learning and convolutional neural networks (CNN). The datasets used in this study include aerial imagery from PTPN 4's Adolina Plantation and the open-source Roboflow Universe dataset, which contain labeled trees categorized by their respective classes. These datasets were preprocessed and augmented to balance the class distribution. Finally, the model was evaluated using metrics such as precision, recall, and mean average precision (mAP). The small variant offers a high precision (0.944) with the highest recall (0.960) and mAP50 (0.978) with a total processing time of 2.2 ms. The results demonstrate that the developed model can accurately detect and classify the different conditions of palm oil trees , providing an effective solution for real-time agricultural monitoring and serving as a valuable tool for analyzing aerial imagery in oil palm plantations to enhance pest detection and management practices in large-scale plantations.

articleTitle: System Protection Hoisting Quayside Container Crane Using IoT Based Brake Resistor Stability
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Crane is equipment used to transfer container or general cargo from ship to shore. An engine generator is used as the main power supply on the crane. A large amount of power is required when lifting. However, when the crane is hoisting down a brake resistor with a large capacity is needed to dissipate the power in the form of heat generated from the downward movement when crane operated. The risk of brake resistor performance failure can occur when the crane moves down with a large load, which will cause reverse power that can damage the engine generator. The performance of the brake resistor is tested in several experiments based on data from crane monitoring system and additional sensor temperature and vibration on motor. The research results show that temperatures above 148°C have a strong correlation with failure risk. A prediction model with decision tree and random forest is developed and result in prediction accuracy of 83.3%. With the implementation of this monitoring system, predictive maintenance can be carried out to prevent downtime and improve crane operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Development of a Portable Face Recognition System with GPS Integration Using Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Face recognition systems are a rapidly evolving computer vision technology capable of accurately identifying faces. Additionally, the development of SBCs (Single Board Computers) has advanced significantly, enabling fast computational processing. The integration of face recognition systems on SBCs enables the creation of embedded face recognition systems. With the addition of GPS devices, it is possible to develop a mobile embedded face recognition system, which can contribute to enhancing infrastructure security and sustainability. This research demonstrates that A portable face recognition system based on Raspberry Pi 5 and a GPS module has been successfully developed. The system successfully detects target faces and able to send location coordinates through the Telegram application. Testing results show that the system's effective range is 1 to 4 meters, with an effective angle of 80° to 100° (from the left horizontal). The tests also indicate that systems without video output generally have higher FPS compared to systems displaying video.

articleTitle: Stacking Ensemble Using Transformer Encoder and NeuralProphet for Indonesian Stock Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Estimating future stock prices has always been a crucial goal in finance. However, accurately predicting stock prices remains a challenge due to their complex and volatile nature. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel hybrid model called NP-Trans. The proposed model combines Transformer Encoder and NeuralProphet by using stacking ensemble. Moreover, strengths of each base model are combined to enhance prediction accuracy. The dataset comprises daily stock prices of prominent Indonesian companies in the LQ45 index such as BBCA, BMRI, and BBRI. The dataset spans from 31 May 2019 to 30 May 2024. Predictive performance is evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and R-squared. On top of that, NP-Tran’s performance will be evaluated with its base and standalone models (Transformer and NeuralProphet). The results demonstrate that NP-Trans consistently outperforms its base and standalone models across all metrics. For BBCA and BBRI, the hybrid model reduces MAE and RMSE by up to 40% and 42%, respectively, while improving R-squared by up to 42%. In conclusion, NP-Trans offers a reliable and accurate tool for financial analysis.

articleTitle: Fetal Heart Rate Data Augmentation Using DCGAN for Multiclass Classification in Normal, Suspected, and Pathological Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study presents a Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (DCGAN) with multiclass classifiers for fetal heart rate (FHR) classification, focusing on imbalanced data between normal, suspected, and pathological cases. Using the CTU-UHB dataset, this study yielded model performance in terms of precision, recall, F1 score, and overall accuracy. The DCGAN model successfully improved the class balance, particularly for the underrepresented pathological cases. The model classification achieved high accuracy (0.97), with strong performance in detecting ‘Normal’ and ‘Fetal Distress’ cases, although the precision for the ‘suspected’ class was slightly lower (0.90). The other graphs also show significant results, especially the detection accuracy and loss, the higher the epoch, the closer the accuracy is to 1.00 and the loss is to 0.00. The confusion matrix results obtained 328 ‘normal’ data, 60 ‘suspect’ data and 27 ‘pathology’ data. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of DCGAN in reducing data imbalance while maintaining high classification accuracy, thus showing potential for improving foetal hypoxia detection in medical applications.

articleTitle: Evaluating The Modularity of Domain-Driven Design Approach: A Case Study of Academic Information System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The shift towards modular architectures, such as modular monoliths and microservices, has gained momentum for their ability to enhance quality attributes of software. Converting to modular structures requires effective decomposition strategies such as Domain-Driven Design (DDD). This study evaluates the effectiveness of DDD in enhancing modularity within academic information systems. Metrics, including Lack of Cohesion Metric (LCOM), Service Granularity Metric (SGM), Number of Operations (NOO), Relational Cohesion (H), and Instability (I), are employed to measure modularity in terms of cohesion, granularity, and stability. Results show that the modules generally exhibit external cohesion but reveal challenges in internal relational cohesion. Fine-grained operations in specific modules yielded an average SGM value of 0.18, indicating that the services were too granular. Additionally, the low ALCOM value of 0.14 demonstrates strong cohesion from an external perspective. However, a low H score of 0.38, 0.35, and 0.21 reveals that inter-type connections must be increased. Furthermore, the system's structure limits static coupling analysis due to Go's internal package structure. This research contributes insights into DDD's effectiveness in enhancing modularity and highlights potential areas for further refinement in architecture.

articleTitle: MRAH-Net: Multiscale Residual Attention Half-UNet Efficient Deep Learning Model for Automatic Polyp Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major global health problem. Early detection through colonoscopy has become very important. However, manual colonoscopy is time-consuming and prone to errors. This has led to efforts to automate polyp detection. One approach that can be used is deep learning. This approach improves diagnostic efficiency and accuracy, which can help doctors while reducing human error. Challenges such as polyp shape, size, texture, and unclear boundaries complicate the segmentation task. Although existing neural networks achieve good accuracy, they often have high memory requirements due to the large number of parameters. To address this, the authors propose Multiscale Residual Attention Half-UNet (MRAH-Net), an enhancement of Half-UNet, which incorporates the Multiscale Residual Attention module to improve performance. Tested on the CVC-ClinicDB dataset, MRAH-Net shows superior accuracy (F1-Score: 94.37%, IoU: 89.61%) with only 251,122 parameters. MRAH-Net outperforms models such as U-Net, ResU-Net++, Double U-Net, and others in terms of accuracy and memory efficiency.

articleTitle: Analysis of Frequency Difference of Arrival (FDoA) Method for Detecting Sound Direction On Gunshot Locater
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The Free Papua Movement carried out by the Free Papua Organization OPM is very detrimental to the Indonesian state and the community around the scene of the incident, many detrimental actions such as arson and shooting of civilians and members of the TNI/POLRI. This research aims to apply sound signal detection technology in detecting the direction of gunfire in Papua carried out by the Free Papua Movement from the Free Papua Organization (OPM). The conflict caused great losses to the country and local communities. By using the Frequency Difference of Arrival (FDoA) method, it is hoped that it can help in preventing yourself from getting close to the source of the gunshot. From the results of the study, Mic 2 had the highest frequency in Experiment 1 of 365,015 Hz and a Doppler shift of 354,689 Hz, indicating that the sound source was close to the microphone. Mic 2 also recorded the highest average SNR of 12,436 dB and the lowest MSE of 0,260, indicating good ability to capture signals with minimal noise and accurate reproduction. In contrast, Mic 3 showed less than satisfactory performance with the highest MSE of 0.898. These findings confirm that Mic 2 is the most effective microphone for use in voice direction detection using the FDoA method, making an important contribution to the development of a more efficient and accurate voice detection system in the context of conflict in Papua.

articleTitle: Compact Deep Learning for Calibrating pH Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The pH value plays the highest role in water quality because good water pH quality will improve the welfare and growth of fish. Therefore, pH monitoring should be conducted routinely, but it is impossible to do manually. Electronic circuits equipped with pH sensors using glass electrodes detect the pH level of water by generating a voltage. However, this voltage is not in line with the standard pH value. This study proposes Compact Deep Learning for Calibration (CDLC) using 12 layers of Artificial Neural Network and some residual layers as a deep learning model to map sensor voltage to pH value. We used 60 data only in this study. Nonetheless, the model achieved better training results with data augmentation. The experimental results show that CDLC outperforms the regression results by other models with a Mean of Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0006. Therefore, CDLC is the right model to implement to regress sensor data into pH.

articleTitle: Mapping Indonesia’s Regions Based on Carbon Emissions Using the K-Means Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Carbon emissions, also known as greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, refer to the release of gases that trap heat in the Earth’s atmosphere, contributing to the greenhouse effect and climate change. These gases, primarily carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), methane (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>), and nitrous oxide (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O) are produced through various human activities. GHGs are generated from sectors such as energy, industry, agriculture, forestry, and waste, each contributing emissions with distinct characteristics in every region. GHG data from 34 provinces in Indonesia from 2000 to 2023 were processed using the K-Means algorithm for clustering to facilitate the analysis of emission patterns, Clustering was based on the similarity of emission characteristics across these five sectors. Clustering results were evaluated using the Silhouette Coefficient to assess the quality of the grouping. Visualization in an inter-active map allows users to understand the distribution patterns of emissions between provinces. The analysis process includes several stages from steps of data collection, data preprocessing, clustering, evaluation, and visualization. The K-Means algorithm has proven effective in grouping provinces based on the similarity of GHG emission profiles in each sector as well as combined sectors. Evaluation using the Silhouette Coefficient showed that clustering data into three clusters obtained an average score of 0.62. This result indicates a medium level of similarity among provinces within a cluster. Riau Province was identified as the highest emitter, while Papua and West Papua were recognized as the provinces acting as the highest absorbers. The interactive map successfully demonstrated the spatial distribution of emissions.

articleTitle: BERT For Classifying Intent in Ulos Fabric and Batak Culture Learning Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Indonesia is rich in cultural heritage, including its woven fabric known as "tenun." Each province has a unique tenun style, but North Sumatra is renowned for its Tenun Ulos. Ulos, a traditional cloth woven by Batak women, features patterns and colors with specific meanings and plays a vital role in Batak ceremonies and traditions. Preservation of Ulos fabric is important, typically achieved through interviews with cultural figures and literary sources. However, fragmented information, inconsistencies, and language barriers hinder effective knowledge dissemination. To address these issues, leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) technology, specifically chatbots presents a promising solution. A chatbot simulates human communication by providing quick, relevant responses through text or voice. The ability to distinguish between names and types of Ulos is essential to reducing confusion about Ulos terminology. For instance, Ulos Pargomgom, worn by elders, varies by occasion, using Ulos Ragidup for weddings and Ulos Suri-Suri Ganjang for naming ceremonies. Identifying users' specific purposes is critical in question-answering and dialogue systems. BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), a deep learning-based language model, excels in providing universal text representation, making it valuable for automated natural language processing. This research evaluates BERT for intent classification by training it on an Ulos and Batak Culture dataset to create an intent classification model. The model achieved an accuracy of 0.83 and an F1 score of 0.83 during training. End-to-end evaluation tested the chatbot's performance, resulting in an accuracy of 85% and an F1 score of 84%. These results indicate that while the model performs reasonably well, there is room for improvement.

articleTitle: Prediction of Cyclotron Ion Source Output using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The consistency of cyclotron ion source output is crucial for ensuring high-quality radioactive isotope production, such as fluorine-18, which is widely used in positron emission tomography (PET) for cancer diagnosis. This study aims to develop a predictive model for cyclotron ion source output using deep neural networks (DNN). The model was trained on historical operational data from the Cyclotron at Dharmais Cancer Hospital, including variables such as ion source voltage, ion source current, bias voltage, bias current, gas flow, high vacuum, and magnetism. The DNN effectively captured the complex non-linear relationships among these parameters, overcoming the limitations of traditional physical models and linear methods. Evaluation results showed great performance, with a test MSE of 0.00178 and an MAE of 0.03064, demonstrating the model’s ability to provide accurate predictions. The findings highlight the potential of DNN for improving cyclotron efficiency and reliability, contributing to better outcomes in nuclear medicine services.

articleTitle: Application of Deep Learning in ECG Signal Classification: Comparison of CNN, LSTM, and Hybrid Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In this paper, the application of deep learning for ECG signal classification is discussed. Three different approaches, namely Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Hybrid CNN-LSTM, are developed and compared. The ECG dataset from PhysioNet is used for the development of the three approaches. The dataset consists of 162 ECG recordings classified into three diagnostic categories: ARR (arrhythmia), CHF (congestive heart failure), and NSR (normal sinus rhythm). The comparisons are evaluated based on performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-Score. The results show that the hybrid method achieved the best performance with an accuracy of 82.60% and an F1-Score of 93.75%, combining CNN's strengths in spatial analysis and LSTM's strengths in temporal patterns. However, detecting minority classes such as CHF remains a challenge. This study highlights the potential of deep learning to support efficient and accurate ECG-based diagnoses and emphasizes the need for further optimization to enhance performance.

articleTitle: Analysis Of Normalize Least Mean Square (NLMS) Method For Gunshot Denoising Process
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In this modern era, the use of gunshot detection devices will be very helpful in the TNI-Polri’s efforts to secure the region. However, gunshots are often mixed with ambient sound or what is commonly referred to as noise. This noise can interfere with the process of determining the direction of gunfire, so a filtering method called denoising is needed to reduce or even eliminate the noise. The noise filtering method used is called Normalize Least Mean Square (NLMS). NLMS is an adaptive filter that can suppress noise from signals affected by noise. The purpose of this study is to obtain an analysis based on the use of NLMS in gunshot sound processing. Based on the results obtained, the average value of SNR in each experiment varies depending on the distance of the sound capture and repetition of data collection. The closer the distance between the sound source and the microphone will have a relatively higher SNR value compared to the distance between the sound source and the microphone. The average value of SNR (Signal to Noise Ratio) obtained is quite good with a value of more than 10 dB. The average value of MSE (Mean Square Error) obtained in each experiment also changes depending on the distance and number of repetitions of data collection. The average MSE value obtained in this study is quite good with an average value close to 0.

articleTitle: Fraud and Anomaly Detection Model in Digital Transactions Based One-Class Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In the current digital era, fraud and anomalies in digital transactions have become a major challenge for financial security. This research proposes the development of a fraud and anomaly detection model for digital transactions using the One-Class Support Vector Machine method. (OC-SVM). The OC-SVM model was chosen for its ability to identify unusual data in environments with imbalanced data distribution. This study begins with an in-depth analysis of the factors and patterns related to digital transactions, followed by dataset preprocessing using a statistical approach. The OC-SVM model was then built and optimized using the Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation technique to improve detection accuracy. The tested detection model performed well with an overall accuracy of (0.72). This indicates that the model is capable of making correct predictions in 72% of all cases. The model has a high recall for detecting fraud (1.00), which means it is very effective in identifying fraud cases. However, the precision for fraud is lower (0.64), which indicates that when the model predicts fraud, 64% of those predictions are correct. High recall with moderate precision results in a good F1-score (0.78) for the fraud class. An AUC-ROC of 0.91 indicates that the model has a high ability to distinguish between fraudulent and non-fraudulent transactions. The training time was recorded at approximately 0.3324 seconds, and the prediction time was only 0.0005 seconds.

articleTitle: Performance with Feature Selection Based Machine Learning: Combination of Low Variance Filter Pearson Correlation for Bots and Brute Force
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This research examines the efficacy of selection feature selection based machine-learning by combining low variance filter, Pearson correlation low variance filter algorithms to detect Bot and Brute Force attacks. The research uses CSE-CIC-IDS2018 dataset and employs a systematic methodology that includes normalization, data cleaning, and equal-size sampling. Through the implementation of low variance filtering with a 0.016 threshold followed by Pearson correlation analysis, the research achieved significant feature reduction while maintaining high classification accuracy. The experimental results demonstrate that for Bot detection, reducing features from 80 to 21 yielded 100% accuracy on threshold 0.1 and threshold 0.2. In Brute Force-Web attack detection, utilizing 57 selected features achieved 99.3% accuracy on threshold 0.4, while SSH-Brute Force detection maintained overall 100% accuracy with only 15 features. Performance evaluation using Decision Tree classification revealed consistently high precision and recall values across all attack types. The findings confirm that the proposed feature selection methodology effectively optimizes intrusion detection systems by identifying the most relevant features while reducing computational complexity without compromising detection capabilities. Future work is recommended to experiment develop real-time predictions for combine ML models with deep learning in the future.

articleTitle: Comparison of Deep Learning Algorithms (LSTM & GRU) for Predicting Product Stocks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The retail sales sector plays a significant role in the global economy, contributing over 15% of global GDP. The rapid growth of e-commerce has made business forecasting increasingly crucial for-profit planning and operational management in the retail sector. Inaccurate predictions can lead to either stock shortages or excess inventory. If demand is underestimated, stockouts may occur, resulting in lost revenue that often cannot be recovered, as dissatisfied customers may turn to other retail options. This research aims to compare the performance of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) algorithms for sales prediction. The methodology involves data collection from sales databases, data preprocessing, and stock prediction using the LSTM and GRU algorithms. The model results are then denormalized, and algorithm performance is evaluated. Findings indicate that the LSTM algorithm outperforms GRU regarding RMSE, MAE, and MAPE, demonstrating greater accuracy in the dataset used. Specifically, LSTM achieved an R² of 0.83, explaining 83% of the data variance, while GRU achieved an R² of 0.70. While both algorithms are effective, GRU's performance is slightly weaker compared to LSTM.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Hybrid PV/Wind/Diesel Power Plant on 60m Patrol Boat
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Hybrid power system considering renewable energy sources is an attempt to reduce the fuel oil consumption during ship’s operation which relied on diesel generator. Photovoltaic (PV) is selected as solar energy is abundant in Indonesia while wind energy has higher potential on ship compared on ground as the received wind speed is higher due to the ship movement. Three design scenarios are evaluated within this research. The difference of each scenario is the size of the renewable energy sources based on the available space on the deck. The first scenario involves installing 40 panels without wind turbine. The second scenario is maximizing all the allocated space to 2 wind turbines, while the last scenario is combining both. All the scenario doesn’t consider the energy saving device as the patrol boat is designed to be operated during the day. The numerical analysis shows that the third scenario, with 36 PVs and 2 wind turbines, may save 11% of fuel consumption annually.

articleTitle: Comparison of Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Methods for Meteorological Data Prediction in Nusa Tenggara
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study compares Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) for forecasting the meteorological data in Nusa Tenggara, on some variables i.e., temperature, rainfall, wind speed, and humidity. It used historical data from 1980 to 2023 from the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency in Indonesia. This research evaluates the performance of both methods based on accuracy and computational efficiency. The SVR demonstrated faster training times, making it suitable for applications requiring quick predictions. Meanwhile, the LSTM excels in capturing complex temporal patterns. SVR and LSTM achieved a maximum R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.633 for forecasting average temperature, indicating similar performance. The findings provide insights into choosing the appropriate model based on specific use cases in meteorology.

articleTitle: Analysis of Indonesian Language Chatbot Using BERT Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Indonesian is the national language used by the Indonesian people. In technology development, technologies such as artificial intelligence-based chatbots have emerged that can answer the questions asked. The creation of an Indonesian-based chatbot requires significant resources to produce quality models. However, with limited resources, a solution is needed to overcome this problem, one of which is to use pre-trained models in NLP, such as BERT, through transfer learning techniques. This study aims to analyze the Indonesian chatbot model for a small scope with limited resources using the pre-trained BERT model. BERT is applied in the training process to produce an optimal chatbot model, evaluate, and obtain accuracy, precision, recall, f1-score, and EM values of 0.97, 0.89, 0.96, 0.92, and 0.87, respectively. In the model test answering the given questions, quite good results were obtained with accuracy, precision, recall, f1-score, and EM values of 0.86, 1, 0.86, 0.92, and 0.86, respectively. The test results show that the BERT architecture can create an Indonesian chatbot model.

articleTitle: Analysis Of Optic Network Design In Housing Using X-GPON, Case Study : Griya Permata Gedangan Housing, Sidoarjo
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This research focuses on planning a 10-Gigabit Capable Passive Optical Network (X-GPON) network in Griya Permata Gedangan Housing, Sidoarjo, to increase the capacity and efficiency of the telecommunications network. With rapid population growth, telecommunication infrastructure that supports high-speed and stable internet access is needed. The network design was carried out through simulation using Google Earth, including plotting the housing area, pulling feeder cables from STO Gedangan to ODCs in housing, and determining the number of ODCs and ODPs. In addition, the research includes the calculation of Power Link Budget and Rise Time Budget to ensure network feasibility. The calculation results show that the power link budget analysis achieves an attenuation of 9.6785 dB and a receiving power of - 12.6785 dBm. These results meet the ITU-T G.987 standard, which requires values below 28 dB for attenuation and -28 dBm for receiving power. In the Rise Time Budget calculation, the tsystem value is 0.0362 ns (36 ps), which meets the maximum requirement of 70 ps. In conclusion, the X-GPON network design is feasible to be implemented in Griya Permata Gedangan Housing to meet the needs of a stable and fast internet.

articleTitle: DST: GPS Tracker for Outdoor Activities of Children with Down Syndrome Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In Indonesia, communities such as Persatuan Orang Tua Anak dengan Down Syndrome (POTADS) play an essential role in assisting people with down syndrome. According to parents at POTADS, children with down syndrome frequently get lost if they are not supervised. Therefore, this research was conducted to monitor children with down syndrome if they are not under the supervision of their parents. This research created an innovative GPS tracker integrated with a mobile phone that uses MQTT as a data transmission protocol. MQTT has real-time characteristics so that parents can monitor their children regularly. The GPS tracker is placed on the vest, the color and material of the vest are designed and adjusted to the preferences and comfort of children with down syndrome. Experimental results show that the device’s accuracy for outdoor use reaches an average of 4.33 meters and 8.36 meters for semi-outdoor use. The battery life of the GPS tracker for outdoor use lasts for 1 hour 15 minutes and for semi-outdoor use lasts 1 hour 45 minutes. For memory usage limit on mobile application is 128,6 MB and the execution time of the tracking feature is below 3,133 ms.

articleTitle: Wavelet Transform and Brain Mapping for EEG-Based Analysis of Brain Activity During Naps
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: "This study investigates the impact of napping on brain activity using Electroencephalogram (EEG) data processed with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and analyzed through brain mapping. EEG offers high temporal resolution and cost efficiency, making it a reliable tool for understanding brain dynamics during naps. Ten subjects, equally divided by gender, participated in a 20-minute nap session while seated in a relaxed position. DWT was applied to remove noise and artifacts, enabling a detailed analysis of brain activity. The findings revealed a significant reduction in brain activity after 10 minutes of napping, supported by consistent patterns in brain mapping, except in subjects experiencing disruptions in relaxation. Although a 20-minute nap is insufficient for a full sleep cycle, it effectively reduces brain activity, suggesting potential cognitive recovery benefits. This research highlights the utility of EEG and wavelet transform in short-duration sleep studies.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Models in Predicting Heart Failure Based on Patient Data: Evaluating the Accuracy and Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Heart failure represents a significant global health challenge, resulting in considerable morbidity and mortality among patients. Machine learning-based predictive modeling in healthcare offers the possibility of early detection and preventative care, enhancing patient outcomes and alleviating the substantial pressure on healthcare providers. In this study, we selected and evaluated ten machine-learning models for accurate heart failure prediction. We used the UCI heart disease dataset, a comprehensive, clean, and widely utilized dataset in several studies. The results showed that LightGBM is the top-performing model with an accuracy of 88%, precision of 88%, recall of 93%, and F1-score of 90%. This was followed by Random Forest, which achieved an accuracy of 88%, precision of 91%, recall of 87%, and an F1-score of 89%, and XGBoost, with an accuracy of 86%, precision of 91%, recall of 84%, and F1-score of 87%. These findings highlight the opportunity to establish resilient predictive tools to support healthcare practitioners.

articleTitle: Chatbot Helpdesk for Centralized Meter Record Application (ACMT) by PLN using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The Centralized Meter Record Application (ACMT) is a mobile and back-office application used by field meter recording officers. Users often face issues and wait for responses from helpdesk and technical support. This research aims to develop a chatbot model that can assist helpdesk and technical support in answering questions according to standard operating procedures by using deep learning. A chatbot is a computer program designed to interact with humans through text conversations. Deep learning is chosen for chatbot analysis because it excels in understanding and generating human-like language, enabling natural, context-aware, and adaptable interactions. Data is collected from IT Service Management (ITSM) and used for intent creation. TensorFlow is used for machine learning and deep learning, and the model training process uses itertools library to determine the number of neurons in each layer. The model is trained for 90 epochs, achieving an accuracy of 96% with a model size of 209.3 KB. Testing using the Robot Framework showed an accuracy of 80%.

articleTitle: Self-loop Laplacian Formation Control for Linear Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study works on scalable formation control of general linear system agents which based on self-loop Laplacian method. Self-loop Laplacian method for scalable formation is used when it is desired that the initial states of agents and communication topology of agents affects the formation size directly. Proof is provided demonstrating that the self-loop Laplacian matrix shares spectral properties with the standard Laplacian matrix, and the two can be related through a transformation matrix. Existing works on scalable formation mostly focused on single and double integrator agents, particularly where the control input algorithm uses self-loop Laplacian matrix. Extending the work on self-loop Laplacian matrix, this study proposes a control input algorithm for agents in linear system dynamics. The algorithm uses both self-loop Laplacian formulation and general linear system consensus methods, and the stability of the whole system is proven using Lyapunov direct method. Two numerical examples with 4 and 5 agents are shown to verify the result.

articleTitle: Usability of Forecasting Technique for Tackling Stock Price Action Decision
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This paper delves into optimizing long-term investment strategies using Information Technology (IT), addressing a gap where IT tools are often more effective for short-term trading but underutilized for long-term investments. The research proposes an IT-based framework designed to enhance decision-making for long-term investors by comparing the predictive capabilities of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Prophet models. Focusing on stock price forecasting for BBRI and AMMN, the study demonstrates how these models can provide accurate predictions over a one-year period. Comparison between LSTM and Prophet forecasting shows Prophet is more reliable for long-term forecasting result. The findings reveal that predictive models can help investors detect trends and make informed decisions, incorporating strategies like price alerts, dollar-cost averaging, and international diversification. By combining these predictive tools with broader investment strategies, the study offers a comprehensive, risk-mitigating solution for long-term investment planning, enabling investors to better navigate market volatility and optimize their portfolio performance over extended time horizons.

articleTitle: Scaling Kubernetes Architectures for High Availability in Cloud
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The shift from monolithic to microservices architectures has amplified the adoption of containerized applications, driving the need for efficient container orchestration platforms like Kubernetes. This paper presents a high-availability (HA) architecture for Kubernetes deployed on Amazon Web Services (AWS) to ensure seamless and resilient application performance in cloud environments. Key components of this architecture include load balancing, autoscaling, and centralized configuration management. The deployment leverages Amazon RDS for database reliability, Prometheus and Grafana for monitoring, and Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) to dynamically adjust resource allocation. Testing indicates that the system maintains high performance under various load conditions, with minimal downtime and rapid recovery from node failures. The proposed framework offers an adaptable and scalable solution for managing high-demand applications, providing a foundation for future optimizations under extreme user loads. The results shows that the system maintains a high success rate across various user loads and time intervals, with a minor drop under maximum load conditions. This behavior aligns with expected performance scaling in distributed systems, where resource allocation adjustments (Pods and worker nodes) enable high reliability across different user demands.

articleTitle: Advancing HIV Patient Classification Through Contrastive Learning and Angular Distance in Graph Convolutional Networks Applied to Gene Expression Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Accurate classification of HIV patients based on gene expression data is essential for personalized medicine, particularly in optimizing antiretroviral therapy (ART) strategies. This study proposes a novel framework that integrates Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) with contrastive learning and angular distance metrics to enhance classification accuracy in high-dimensional gene expression data. The model involves several stages: data preprocessing to normalize gene expression data, graph construction to represent gene interactions, GCN implementation to extract relational features, contrastive learning to improve feature separability, and the incorporation of angular distance metrics to enhance sensitivity to subtle variations. The combined loss function, integrating cross-entropy and contrastive losses, ensures robust optimization during training. When compared to traditional machine learning methods such as Random Forest, Naive Bayes, K-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machines, and Artificial Neural Networks, the proposed model demonstrated superior 71.22% accuracy, 65.13% precision, and 64.7% recall. Despite these promising results, the study is limited by the relatively small dataset size, which may restrict the model’s ability to generalize across broader patient populations and complex clinical scenarios. Future studies should incorporate larger and more diverse datasets to better capture the heterogeneity of HIV patients and further validate the proposed framework. While computationally intensive, the framework shows promise in advancing HIV patient profiling and guiding personalized treatment strategies, with future work focusing on improving efficiency and interpretability for broader clinical applications.

articleTitle: Comparison of GRU and Random Forest Models in Predicting Meteorological Data on Sumatra Island
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: One of the major challenges for the sustainability of human life is addressing climate change, particularly in tropical regions like Sumatra Island. Predicting meteorological conditions is crucial for mitigating climate change and enhancing adaption efficiency. This study seeks to forecast climate conditions on Sumatra Island utilizing the Gate Recurrent Unit (GRU) algorithm and the Random Forest technique to predict meteorological data. The data utilized were acquired from seven meteorological stations, covering the period from January 1, 2000, to June 30, 2024. The GRU approach was selected due of its potential to manage extensive time series data while minimizing information loss. Random Forest is a solid technique for capturing non-linear correlations in complex data. This study using Streamlit framework web-based simulation, enabling real-time visualization of meteorological. The data preprocessing includes handling missing values with forward and backward filling and normalizing features using min-max scaling. The results reveal that GRU generally beats Random Forest, with the maximum R2 value of 64.7% for the lowest temperature variable. In contrast, the rainfall variable exhibits the lowest accuracy GRU R2 1.2% and 7.2% for Random Forest. Noise and absent values in the dataset compromise the precision of both models. In this work, the GRU demonstrated superior performance in modeling meteorological time series data on the island of Sumatra, both algorithms have limits when dealing with variables that possess inconsistent data properties. This combination of approaches provides a solid foundation for the development of more adaptive prediction models to the challenges of tropical climate data.

articleTitle: Meat Classification Using MobileNetV3Large Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Classification of raw meat is one of the critical challenges in the food industry to ensure product quality and safety. This research aims to develop an effective and efficient classification model using the MobileNetV3Large architecture, known for its high performance and low computing requirements. The dataset consists of three types of raw meat: beef, horse, and pork. The dataset used for training the MobileNetV3Large model was subjected to data augmentation techniques to increase dataset variation and prevent overfitting. The research results show that the proposed model achieved an accuracy of 97.44%, significantly improving compared to other methods such as MobileNet, MobileNetV2, and ViT (Vision Transformer). This model possesses fewer parameters than the Vision Transformer (ViT), yet it demonstrates superior accuracy in meat classification. This success shows the great potential of MobileNetV3Large in image classification applications in the food industry, especially in simplifying and speeding up the raw meat identification process.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Transfer Learning Models Based on Convolutional Neural Networks for Monkeypox Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Monkeypox, a zoonotic disease caused by the Monkeypox virus, has become a significant public health concern due to its potential for rapid human-to-human transmission. Early detection plays a crucial role in effective containment and treatment. This paper presents a computer vision-based approach using deep learning techniques to detect monkeypox through dermatological lesion images. A publicly available dataset from Kaggle, consisting of high-resolution lesion images, was used to evaluate the performance of six pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) models: ResNet50, ResNet101, ResNet152, InceptionResNetV2, VGG16, and VGG19. These models were adapted for binary classification using transfer learning, with pre-trained ImageNet weights and fine-tuning. Among the evaluated models, InceptionResNetV2 achieved the highest performance, with an accuracy of 94.044%, precision of 94.152%, recall of 94.044%, and F1-score of 94.021%. The novelty of this study lies in leveraging multiple deep learning architectures to benchmark monkeypox detection while demonstrating the practicality of transfer learning on a small dataset. This study emphasizes the potential of AI-powered diagnostics in distinguishing monkeypox lesions from other dermatological conditions, providing a reliable and accessible solution for integration into health surveillance systems.

articleTitle: Real-Time Health Monitoring Based ESP8266 and Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study aims to develop a health monitoring system using an ESP8266 microcontroller and fuzzy logic to view real-time health data and predict the patients’ heart health conditions. The system is designed to monitor various physiological data, including heart rate and blood pressure, by utilizing sensors connected to the ESP8266 microcontroller device. Data obtained from the sensors will be transmitted wirelessly to a web-based platform, which facilitates remote monitoring and real-time data visualization. In addition, fuzzy logic is used to analyze the sensor data, classifying the health status into defined categories, including normal, moderate, and critical. This method facilitates a comprehensive understanding of the health situation, which offers patients a precise and clear description of their health status. The results of this study indicate that the combination of ESP8266 with fuzzy logic offers an effective, economical, and scalable solution for real-time health monitoring. This device can be applied for remote patient monitoring and early identification of possible heart disease problems.

articleTitle: Predicting Infectious Diseases Using XGBoost Algorithm and Discovering Dominant Features Using SHAP Model Interpreter
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the performance of the XGBoost algorithm and identify the most significant features in predicting three infectious diseases based on specific geographic clusters: DHF, COVID-19, and Varicella. Understanding the characteristics of these diseases will aid healthcare workers in forecasting patient conditions using historical patient data. The methodology begins with preparing a dataset comprising 68,666 patient visits, including 2,679 patients diagnosed with the three diseases. The data source consists of patient records from a Bandung Regency clinic in the Bojongsoang District, covering three years from January 1, 2019, to December 31, 2021. The dataset was divided into 80% for training and 20% for testing. The primary data source includes keywords related to the characteristics of the three diseases in the medical history data, which were transformed into 19 features. In addition to these 19 features, other data, such as temperature, collected from medical examinations conducted by nurses during registration, were also incorporated. Experiments were performed using RapidMiner with the XGBoost algorithm, followed by an experiment using Python to evaluate the most significant features with the SHAP model interpreter. The results indicated that XGBoost achieved an accuracy of 73.32%, an average recall of 62.28%, and an average precision of 75.22%. Furthermore, the SHAP model interpretation revealed that vCough, vTemp, vSpot, vNauseous, and vFever were the most significant features for predicting the three diseases.

articleTitle: Automatic Bus Route Notification System at Bus Stops Using LoRa SX 1278 and WeMos ESP 32 Modules
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This research aims to develop an automatic bus route notification system at bus stops using LoRa SX 1278 and WeMos ESP32 modules. This research addresses the lack of real-time bus route information at bus stops, which often leads to passenger confusion. This research uses a Research and Development (R&D) methodology, including steps such as identifying potential and problems, data collection, product design, design validation, design revision, and product testing. The results demonstrate that the system effectively delivers real-time bus route information at stops, with a maximum range of 100 meters using the LoRA SX 1278 module. Route information is conveyed through audio playback using DF Player Mini and Speaker and visual display on LCD. This system is expected to improve accessibility, especially for elderly passengers and those with visual or hearing impairments, reduce reliance on manual announcements, and increase efficiency and convenience for Transjakarta transportation users.

articleTitle: Implementation Of Global Positioning System (GPS) Module In Motor-boat Crossing Tracking System Using Lora Communication Protocol
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: South Kalimantan is an archipelagic region characterized by a large number of river systems that flow from the interior to the sea. Rivers function as a source of livelihood and a transportation route for people and goods. Current technological advances and developments is the Internet of Things (IoT). This technology is utilized by creating a system that can monitor the location of motorboats so that community needs can be met. So a system was created that can determine the location, distance, speed and estimated time of arrival of motor boats. This research aims to determine the accuracy of the latitude and longitude coordinate data for motorboats currently operating on the Motorboat Crossing Tracking System and to calculate the distance, speed and estimated time of arrival of motorboats based on GPS coordinate data on the Motorboat Crossing Tracking System and GPS on Android cellphones. This research was carried out using the NodeMCU microcontroller, NEO-6M and Lora modules. The research was carried out for 2 days and it was found that the accuracy of the motor ship's latitude and longitude coordinate data for the first test was 96.96% and the accuracy value for the second test was 93.59%. In calculating the distance, speed, and estimated time of arrival of motor ships, the average error for the distance parameters was 4.8%, speed was 32.9%, and the estimate was 8.1%. So the accuracy value for the distance parameter is 95.2%, speed is 67.1%, and estimation is 91.9%.

articleTitle: Smart Home System Based on IoT Concept Using Multi-Sensor Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The smart home concept is being developed using the Internet of Things (IoT) technology. The smart home concept offers security services such as monitoring dangerous gas leaks and fires, light control, and keyless door lock systems. Previous studies introduced the idea of a smart home system based on IoT depending on security needs and determining the number of sensors. Still, the description of specific devices used needs to be detailed. Thus, a proper design model for a smart home system was required. This paper proposes a prototype design for a smart home concept by integrating multiple sensors. The sensors used in this prototype are the MQ-2 sensor, DHT-11 sensor, flame sensor, LDR sensor, and RFID. The research results show that the multi-sensor integration was successful, and each sensor could function according to its function within a time range from 0.6 seconds to 2 minutes. The prototype can be implemented through mobile-based applications and given quickly and flexibly.

articleTitle: Inspection Study of Tempe Fermentation Cabinet Through Computational Modeling To Determine Temperature And Humidity Distribution
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The fermentation process used in making tempe, which involves the fungus Rhizopus oligosporus, often poses a risk of contamination by pathogenic microbes if not carried out properly. In addition, the use of unclean raw materials or less than optimal sanitation conditions can cause tempe to be unsafe for consumption. In addition, environmental factors are also a concern, such as deforestation caused by high demand for soybeans, the main raw material in making tempe, and the negative impact on environmental sustainability that can occur due to waste disposal from the production process. In overcoming these problems, it is important to prioritize hygienic processing practices, develop innovative technologies to monitor and control product quality. One such technology is the semi-automatic tempe fermentation cabinet. This study discussed about computational modeling to analyze heat transfer and humidity in the fermentation process. The simulation results show that in a fermentation time of 30 hours, the temperature inside the cabinet is in the range of 33 - 34 degrees C. Humidity values are in the range of 58 - 66%.
