The highest temperature is in the heating element blower area at 192.87 deg C.

articleTitle: Performance of Feature Extraction Techniques using CC-PEV and Subtractive Pixel Adjacency Matrix in Machine Learning-Based Steganalysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Steganalysis involves detecting hidden messages embedded within cover objects, such as images, audio, or video. This paper presents a universal steganalysis method aimed at countering the most widely used spatial-domain steganography techniques. The proposed model leverages support vector machines (SVM) to classify stego images based on extracted features. To evaluate the model’s effectiveness, we applied various feature extraction techniques and tested the steganalysis approach on a dataset of stego images. Our results show that the proposed method achieves robust performance in detecting stego images across different scenarios. Specifically, the model with the linear kernel and SPAM features yielded the highest detection accuracy, with an average of 75.28%. In contrast, the combination of the Gaussian kernel and CC-PEV features was less effective, achieving a lower detection accuracy of only 66.95%. These findings highlight the importance of selecting the right kernel and feature extraction method for optimal steganalysis performance. The study also suggests that while the linear kernel with SPAM features provides stable and reliable results, more complex methods like the Gaussian kernel require further refinement for better accuracy. Overall, this paper offers valuable insights into the effectiveness of different steganalysis techniques for combating modern steganography methods.

articleTitle: Digital Reconstruction of Historical Artworks Using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionized various domains, including the restoration and digital reconstruction of historical artworks. This paper explores how AI technologies—specifically deep learning, image processing, and neural networks—are employed to digitally reconstruct and restore damaged or incomplete historical artworks. By enhancing images, filling in missing sections, and generating data-driven reconstructions, AI offers new possibilities for art preservation and accessibility. Challenges, limitations, and ethical considerations in using AI for artistic restoration are also addressed. The study concludes with an outlook on the future of AI-driven art reconstruction, emphasizing its significance for cultural heritage preservation.

articleTitle: Analysis Of Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) Method For Direction Detection In Gunshot Locator
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Incidents of mass shootings and missed shots by irresponsible parties often occur in densely populated areas, increasing the risk to public safety. This research aims to develop an effective method of localizing the origin of gunfire, to support both military and civilian efforts in identifying the perpetrator. A gunshot direction detection system is proposed as an innovation capable of determining the location of the sound source and improving communication efficiency. This research uses the Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR) method for gunshot localization. By minimizing the noise variance, MVDR improves the clarity of the received gunshot sound and improves the accuracy of the Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation. The effectiveness of the MVDR algorithm is evaluated using signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and Mean Square Error (MSE) parameters as accuracy parameters. The results show that the MVDR method has a DoA estimation accuracy rate of 96.29% which proves the potential of MVDR as a reliable algorithm for voice localization in noisy environments. This study makes significant contributions to the development of more advanced localization systems, so as to improve public safety and situational awareness in critical situations.

articleTitle: Maximum Depth Parameter Explorations of Random Forest Method For Breast Cancer Classification On RNA Mutations Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: One kind of cancer that affects women globally is breast cancer. Machine learning techniques are a possible alternative approach to increase the precision of breast cancer detection. One popular technique that can handle the complexity of genetic data is Random Forest. The purpose of this study is to investigate how changes in the maximum depth parameter affect the Random Forest method’s ability to classify breast cancer using RNA mutations data. This study uses METABRIC RNA Mutations dataset that is processed through feature selection process to ensure the most relevant features for classification. Experiments were conducted by applying various maximum depth values to the Random Forest model and measuring its performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The results showed that variations in the maximum depth parameter had a significant effect on model performance, where the optimal maximum depth value can substantially increase classification accuracy. These findings provide valuable insights into the use of Random Forest for breast cancer classification, especially in setting appropriate parameters to improve prediction accuracy based on gene expression.

articleTitle: Digital Satellite Image-Based Automatic Building Segmentation Using Pixel Attention Half-UNet
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Building detection is important in geographic information updates and urban and regional planning. Building detection is more efficient when done automatically. However, automatic building detection is still a challenge in Geoinformatics. Buildings with the same colour, texture, and shape as their surroundings pose a challenge in automatic building detection. Due to their complexity, some traditional methods for automatic building detection do not have optimal performance. A neural network method called Pixel Attention Half-UNet is proposed to overcome this challenge. The proposed method is based on the Half-UNet framework, utilizing Pixel Attention. Pixel Attention Half-UNet was trained and tested using high-resolution satellite images from the Massachusetts Buildings Dataset. The proposed method gives F1-Score and Intersection-over-Union (IoU) results of 82.95% and 70.94%, respectively. The proposed method performs better than previous methods, namely DeepLabv3+ (Xception), RefineNet (ResNet50), U-Net, Half-UNet, SegNet, and Bayesian-SegNet. This method also provides a lower parameter, which is 0.26 million.

articleTitle: Distributed Denial of Service Attack Detection Model with Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: One of the most prevalent cyber-attacks today is Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS). Today, many network administrators still rely on manual analysis to detect suspicious activity with the help of IDS (Intrusion Detection System) and IPS (Intrusion Prevention System). This method involves a detailed review of transaction logs and network activity. Although effective in some cases, manual analysis requires a long time and high accuracy, which is not practical for large and complex network environments. This research aims to develop an accurate DDoS attack detection model on computer networks using Machine Learning method with Random Forest algorithm. Through data analysis of the CICDDoS2019 dataset, especially the UDP (User Datagram Protocol) flooding attack type. Based on the evaluation results, the Random Forest-based DDoS attack detection model shows very high effectiveness, especially in identifying DrDoS_UDP attacks. With an accuracy of 99.99%, precision of 98.86%, and recall of 97.36%, this model is able to correctly distinguish between benign data and attack data. The cross-validation results also show the consistency of the model's performance, with an average accuracy of 99.96% and a very small variance. The model successfully detects attacks with good precision and balance, evidenced by the high F1-Score value of 98.10%, as well as superior performance in detecting DrDoS_UDP and BENIGN classes.

articleTitle: Structure Analysis of Vacuum Pressure Pan to Evaluate Stress Area Based Modelling Method
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In parametric modeling, the rules and images that form the shape of an object depend on what the user needs. The benefit of the parametric model is that the user can modify the design of the intended object just by adjusting its parameters without needing to redraw it. In this study, most concerned at stress allocation at vacuum pressure pan. Drying with vacuum pressure the aspect mechanisms that expend the greatest quantity of energy, derived to the considerable potential energy required for the conversion to vapor of water. The result showed Stress inside and outside range of the pan could be handle, so that means it is still safe range. The vacuum pressure at -15 inHg the stress occurred in pan area is about 2.985 – 22.657 Mpa. Then when the vacuum pressure at -20 inHg the stress occurred in pan area is about 4.0859 – 31.004Mpa. Then when the vacuum pressure at -25 inHg the stress occurred in pan area is about 5.185 – 39.351 Mpa

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Random Forest, SVM, and SVM-Hypertuning Methods on Concept Map Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: A concept map is a visual tool used to illustrate the relationships between concepts in a domain of knowledge. In an educational context, concept maps play an important role in helping students understand the structure of knowledge and the relationships between ideas. With the increasing adoption of technology in learning, analyzing concept map data is becoming increasingly relevant to evaluate student understanding and support the decision-making process. This study compares three machine learning methods, namely Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and SVM with parameter hypertuning (SVM-Hypertuning), in the classification of concept map data. The data used is represented in the form of structural and semantic features of student concept maps. Performance evaluation was conducted using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. The results show that the SVM-Hypertuning method has the best performance compared to RF and standard SVM, with accuracy reaching 91.2%. This research makes an important contribution to the development of analytic models to improve the effectiveness of data-driven educational evaluation.

articleTitle: Coverage Planning Of 5G New Radio Network Planning With 1.8 GHz Frequency In Balikpapan City
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study aims to start the planning stage or the deployment of 5G New Radio (NR) technology, especially in Balikpapan city. The main focus is on 5G NR network planning, particularly for a coverage area of 511.01 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in the 1.8 GHz (1800 MHz) frequency band. This initiative aims to position East Balikpapan as a premier industrial hub in Kalimantan. The propagation model used for this research study is the 5G NR Urban Macro (UMa) model, which is adapted to the 3GPP TR 38.900 standard. Simulations were conducted using Atoll software, resulting in a path loss value of 110.4824905 dB and a cell radius of 1194.95 meters. To build a strong network service, about 70 sites are required. The downlink simulation resulted in an RSRP (Synchronization Signal - Reference Signal Received Power) parameter value of -70.76 dBm, while the SS-SINR (Synchronization Signal - Signal to Interference plus Noise Ratio) parameter was measured at 28.65 dB throughput achieved was 250 Mbps.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of YouTube Culinary Content on "WNK" Restaurant Using Text Mining Technique with VADER
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In this paper, the application of the Valence Aware Dictionary for Sentiment Reasoning (VADER) model on Indonesian-language comments on YouTube discussing culinary content about "WNK" restaurant is discussed. The study evaluates two approaches, the VADER Default model and the Customized VADER model tailored for the Indonesian language, using 7,834 comments collected from three selected YouTube creators. Results show that the VADER Default model achieved a higher accuracy of 92.21%, compared to 76.63% for the VADER Custom model. However, the VADER Default model exhibited bias toward the neutral category, making it less effective in classifying positive and negative sentiments in Indonesian comments. Conversely, the VADER Custom model produced a more balanced sentiment distribution, with a Precision of 76.94%, Recall of 76.48%, and an F1-score of 76.68%. These findings suggest that the VADER Custom model is more effective for understanding Indonesian sentiments, highlighting its significant potential for Indonesian text sentiment analysis, particularly in the culinary sector.

articleTitle: Detection Model Development for Chili Leaves Disease Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Chili plants are the main horticultural commodity in Indonesia, with dominant production in the agricultural sector. Data from the Central Statistics Agency (BPS) from 2021 to 2023 shows that chili is consistently in the top five vegetable productions. However, production is often hampered by diseases caused by pathogenic microorganisms, so disease identification is very important. The current method performed by chili farmers is based on visual inspection of chili leaves, which is considered subjective from one individual to another. This study produces primary data in the form of images of chili leaves in five classes, namely healthy leaves, curly leaves, yellow virus leaves, spotted leaves, and whitefly leaves which have been published in Roboflow. Through six times of dataset training of the deep learning model using YoloV8, the best model was obtained with an Average Precision (AP) value at Intersection over Union 0.5 and 0.5-0.95 of 85.1% and 67.3%, respectively. This model is optimal for applications that require fast and accurate results.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Sentiment Analysis of ChatGPT App Reviews Using Lexicon-Based Methods, Deep Learning, and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In the current era, many AI chatbot applications are widely used by people. One of the most popular among these is ChatGPT. Due to its application-based platform, ChatGPT has received a large volume of user feedback. This study aims to analyze these user comments through sentiment analysis with also implementing a combination of machine learning and deep learning models. For traditional machine learning the models are such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, XGBoost, and CatBoost. Meanwhile, for the deep learning this study implementing BERT, RoBERTa, XLNet, and GPT- 2. The dataset used in this study is qualitative and was sourced from Google Play Web. Each of the model will perform and evaluated by the accuracy, precision, F1-Score, and recall. This study finds that the GPT-2 model, as one of the deep learning approaches, provided the best performance in this study because can prove excellent performance, efficiency, effectiveness and accuracy compared to other existing models

articleTitle: Comparison of Prostate Cell Image Classification Using CNN; Xception and DenseNet-201
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Prostate cancer is the second highest cause of cancer deaths in men in the United States, with an estimated 34,700 deaths from this disease in 2023. Until now, the causes of this cancer are still unknown compared to other cancers. Several factors that can influence cancer risk include age, ethnicity, genetic factors, and family history. In detecting this disease there are many problems such as lack of accurate diagnosis. To overcome this problem, this research will use artificial intelligence to classify 7 images of prostate cells. The artificial intelligence method used is the CNN method from deep learning which is applied to images of prostate cells. The two CNN models used are Xception and DenseNet-201. There are two tests in this research, namely at the training stage and the testing stage. As a result, at the training stage Xception had higher accuracy results (99.58%) than DenseNet-201 (98.85%). At the training stage, an analysis of the time required for the model in the classification process is also carried out. This process, DenseNet-201 took longer (with an average of 95 minutes) than Xception (with an average of 69 minutes 24 seconds). Apart from training, analysis was also carried out at the testing stage, where Xception also outperformed at this stage with slightly higher accuracy than DenseNet-201 (97.44% (STD ±1.26)>97.32% (STD ±1.49)). Overall, the analysis shows that Xception provides better performance in training and testing than DenseNet-201.

articleTitle: Prediction of Angiotensin-Converting-Enzyme (ACE) Inhibitors as Antihypertensive Agents Using Artificial Neural Network Optimized by Artificial Bee Colony
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study uses a dataset from the ChEMBL database to predict the activity of Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) inhibitors as antihypertensive medicines by use of the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm and Artificial Neural Network (ANN). Although they are time-consuming, expensive, and prone to uncertainty, traditional methods include wet-lab testing are often utilized for ACE inhibitor identification. This study intends to increase predictive performance by including systematic optimization through the ABC algorithm with ANN. Architectural and hyperparameters of ANN models were optimized using the ABC algorithm. With an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.683 on the test set, the model with 10 population size showed the greatest performance among the five models evaluated, therefore proving its efficacy in reflecting the general data pattern. These findings show the possibilities of integrating the ABC algorithm with ANN for precise prediction of ACE inhibitor activity, therefore offering a faster and less expensive substitute for conventional approaches. Larger and more varied datasets are required for more thorough investigation to confirm the generalizability of this method for several drug discovery uses.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in CyberSecurity: Robust RF Model Approach to Accurate Fraud Detection in Credit Card
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In this study, a powerful machine learning model was developed to strengthen cyber security in banking systems by detecting fraud using the European card benchmark dataset. The study addressed the significant challenge of class imbalance through PCA-based comparative analysis, ensuring both efficiency and accuracy. Core methodologies included the use of Multilayer Perceptron, PCA-based Random Forest, and standard Random Forest classifiers, with fine-tuning of hidden layers, learning rates, and epochs to enhance performance. Cross-validation techniques were employed to evaluate model effectiveness and minimize overfitting. Among the tested approaches, the standard Random Forest (RF) classifier proved to be the most effective, achieving an impressive accuracy of 99% and a precision of 98%, with no signs of overfitting. These results highlight the potential of advanced machine learning approaches in improving fraud detection and strengthening cyber security in financial systems. The optimized RF model provides a crucial solution for protecting sensitive transactions and combating fraudulent activities in banking.

articleTitle: Recalibration Parallel Half U-Net for Polyp Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images is a critical task for the early detection and prevention of colorectal cancer, which remains one of the leading causes of cancer- related deaths worldwide. Accurate segmentation of polyps is essential to assist medical professionals in identifying and removing precancerous lesions during routine screening procedures. In this study, we propose the Recalibration Parallel Half U-Net, a novel deep learning architecture based on the Half U-Net framework, designed to enhance segmentation performance through a dual parallel encoder structure. This recalibration mechanism effectively captures multi-scale features and improves the model’s ability to differentiate between polyp and non-polyp regions. Experimental results on the widely used CVC-Clinic dataset demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms traditional U-Net and Half U-Net models, achieving a mean F1-score of 93.63% and a mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 88.47%. These performance gains highlight the robustness and accuracy of our proposed approach, indicating its potential for integration into clinical workflows to support more reliable and efficient polyp detection in colonoscopy procedures.

articleTitle: Analysis for Generalized of Viscoelastic Fluid with Shear-Thickening Fluids
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Non-Newtonian fluids, particularly viscoelastic fluids with rheopectic and shear-thickening behaviors, exhibit complex dynamics influenced by shear rate and time. Rheopectic fluids display a time-dependent viscosity increase under constant shear stress, while shear-thickening fluids respond with viscosity increases at higher shear rates. This study develops and validates advanced mathematical models using COMSOL Multiphysics and Python to simulate these unique behaviors. By modifying the Navier-Stokes equations to account for non-linear, time- and shear-dependent viscosities, the models accurately predict flow behavior under varying conditions. Key findings reveal significant differences in viscosity trends, pressure distribution, and velocity profiles between the two fluid types. These results provide critical insights into optimizing fluid transport processes and designing advanced materials with tailored rheological properties, benefiting fields such as engineering, materials science, and biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Optimization Of KNN, SVM, And SVM Kernel in Water Potability Prediction with Hyperparameter Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This research focuses on optimizing the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and SVM Kernel classification methods using a hyperparameter approach to improve the accuracy of water potability prediction. The water potability dataset containing 3276 water samples with 10 features is used. The research methods include exploratory data analysis (EDA), data preprocessing (handling missing values, standardization, dimensionality reduction, and feature selection), modeling (KNN, SVM, SVM Kernel), hyperparameter optimization using GridSearchCV, and model evaluation (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC AUC). The results show that the SVM model with an optimized RBF kernel has the best performance, but the overall model accuracy is still not optimal. Further research is suggested to address class imbalance, select more relevant features, engineer features, and use ensemble techniques. With further development, it is expected that a more accurate and reliable model for predicting water potability can be produced, thereby contributing to improving public health and well-being.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Optimization Algorithms for Shortest Path Determination on Facial Edge Coordinates
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Optimization is a computational process to find the best solution by minimizing or maximizing an objective function. This research compares the performance of three optimization algorithms Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Simulated Annealing (SA) in determining the shortest path optimization between coordinate points extracted from detected facial edge images. Using the Canny edge detection method, 10 single facial images with a resolution of 120 x 120 pixels were processed to produce (X, Y) coordinates as input for the optimization process. The results show that GA consistently outperforms the other methods, achieving the shortest total distance in 9 out of 10 datasets. The results of the first image data comparison, the GA method produced the shortest total distance with a value of 18,199.59 pixels, while (SA) 21,072.28 pixels had a performance 15.78% worse than GA, and (PSO) 28,381.58 (pixels) showed a performance 55.94% worse than GA. SA showed competitive and optimal results in one dataset, while PSO consistently provided the longest distance, indicating its lower efficiency in this research.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning to Enhance Software Quality Metrics for BMKG’s Website and Application Services
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This research evaluates the website and application of BMKG using software quality metrics techniques that the perfomance have been upgraded by leveraging machine learning. Three process evaluation are implemented for the BMKG website and application: Crash error reports and time delay response from the website, weather forecast accuracy, and user reviews on application. Crash error and time delay response are monitored using an automatic website monitoring tool: UptimeRobot. The quality of the accuracy of weather data forecasts are evaluated by comparing BMKG data with two global platforms, MetNorway and OpenMeteo, using machine learning techniques: MAE, MSE, and R-squared. User feedbacks are retrieved from the last 1000 reviews from the Google Play Store, then analyzed using machine learning techniques: TDF-IF and F1-value. The results of this research indicates several thing that need to be improved from the BMKG website and application: The speed of website response, the accuracy of weather forecast data, and a user interface that is that is easier to use. By implementing these improvements, the positive feedback of users will increase significantly.

articleTitle: 3D Transfer Learning for Lung Nodule Malignancy Binary Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Many studies have focused on classifying lung nodules in CT scans, primarily utilizing 2D approaches. However, CT scans are inherently 3D representations, which presents challenges for traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) designed for 2D images. In this work, a novel combination of 3D transfer learning and batch oversampling was adopted to classify benign and malignant lung nodules using the Lung Nodule Analysis - Intelligent Systems in Medical Imaging (LUNA22-ISMI) dataset. The preprocessing pipeline consisted of excluding indeterminate labeled nodules, clamping patches to the lung window, extracting nodule regions based on diameter, and applying z-score normalization. Batch oversampling with augmentation was implemented for the training set. Multiple models pre-trained on ImageNet with weights adapted for 3D were evaluated using a five-fold cross-validation setup. Notably, EfficientNetB1 achieved the highest overall and balanced metrics on the test sets, surpassing 90% in sensitivity, specificity, precision, and accuracy, highlighting its potential for binary classification of lung nodules. https://github.com/nheryanto/luna22

articleTitle: Digital Shopping Era: Uncovering the Drivers of Electronic Purchase Intentions on E-Commerce
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Consumer purchasing habits have changed dramatically due to recent developments in digital technology and faster internet, with e-commerce emerging as the main channel for buying electronics like laptops, smartphones, and household appliances. Although electronic sales are growing, concerns about product quality, fraud, delivery, and after-sales support still impact consumers' purchase intentions. This research aims to identify factors that influence the intention to purchase electronic products on e-commerce platforms in Indonesia. The factors tested include subject norm, satisfaction, price advantage, information searching, and received risk. The research sample consisted of 200 respondents who actively use e-commerce and have purchased electronic products in the last 6 months. Data collection was carried out through an online survey in October-November 2024. The results of multiple regression analysis show that subject norm, satisfaction, information searching have a significant positive influence on electronic purchase intentions.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of PID-Controlled Single-Input Dual-Output (SIDO) Synchronous Buck Converter Using PLECS
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In industrial world, many mass-produced products require high precision to maintain product quality. To support industrial performance, robots are widely used for high-speed repetitive tasks. The development of a Single-Input Dual-Output (SIDO) buck converter offers a flexible solution for efficiently managing power in robotic devices. The implementation of a PID controller in synchronous buck converters ensures stable output voltages within specified ranges. This study compares two topologies of synchronous buck converters—one without a controller and another employing a PID controller using the SIDO method—simulated using PLECS software. Simulation results with PID control closely approximate the desired voltage drop values. The synchronous buck converter with PID control is proposed as an effective system. PID controllers facilitate faster transient response to achieve desired output voltages with minimal overshoot and can reduce oscillations and instability that may lead to power wastage. In conclusion, this research affirms that a synchronous buck converter with SIDO configuration and PID controller is an efficient solution for applications requiring precise voltage and current regulation, while achieving optimal energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approach with EfficientNet-CBAM for Apple Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Disease attacks have the potential to decrease apple productivity, particularly in Poncokusumo Village, Malang Regency. The manual process of disease identification requires a significant amount of time and specialized knowledge, which results in inefficiency and frequently blocks early treatment. The objective of this research is to create a precise deep learning model for the detection of diseases in apples in order to ensure that it functions effectively in situations that are real. To accomplish this objective, directly collected disease image data on fruits from apple fields in Poncokusumo Village. The EfficientNet model implements the CBAM attention mechanism. The EfficientNet B0 version was employed as the basis for the model for this work, with CBAM being implemented to improve feature extraction and identify infection spots within the image. Based on the research findings, the EfficientNet-CBAM model has an F1 score of 92% and an accuracy of 93.67%. The attention mechanism of the model is effective in identifying infected areas, enabling both quicker and more precise detection. This method has the potential to enhance the precision and efficacy of disease identification, as well as offer producers advantages by applying preventive measures earlier.

articleTitle: Optimizing Production Forecasting in the Automotive Sector through Effective Data Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In the automotive industry, effective data management is essential for ensuring the timely production and delivery of key components. The just-in-time production process, which aligns production with customer demand received one day in advance (H-1), can lead to material shortages and delayed deliveries due to reliance on suppliers. The company's policy against maintaining inventory necessitates precise forecasting of production quantities based on historical data, particularly given the volatile nature of demand patterns. This research aims to develop a data management approach that supports accurate forecasting analyses. By conducting a comparative analysis of various forecasting models, this study seeks to identify the optimal model that yields the lowest Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The findings will provide reliable production estimates for upcoming periods, thereby enhancing production planning and scheduling. Additionally, this study aligns with Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure, by promoting sustainable and resilient production systems through innovative forecasting methods.

articleTitle: Assessing Peatland Fire Vulnerability in Bengkalis with Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Peatland fires have become a significant environmental issue in Indonesia, particularly recurring annually on Sumatra Island's east coast, specifically in Bengkalis Regency. Consequently, there is a need to develop a model for predicting peatland fires. Identifying burn areas is one method to assess peatland fire vulnerability. This study aimed to determine the vulnerability of peatland fires in Bengkalis Regency by utilizing burn area data from MODIS for the year 2019. This research using independent variables such as physiography, physical characteristics of peat, anthropogenic, rainfall and NDMI. The RF model's accuracy was evaluated using the AUC value. In Bengkalis Regency, the total burned area amounted to 175.85 km², with Rupat District exhibiting the largest burned area in the regency. The RF model accurately predicts peatland fires in Bengkalis Regency, achieving an AUC value of 0.979 for the training data and 0.972 for the test data. The five significant predictor variables impacting peatland fires are road density, precipitation, drainage density, NDMI, and river density. The overall accuracy of the predictions is noted to be 95.07%. These results are valuable for enhancing fire management strategies in Bengkalis Regency and can aid authorities in making more informed decisions regarding fire prevention measures.

Index Terms: Accuracy Of The Random Forest Model

articleTitle: Comparison of Cosine Similarity and BM25 in Book Procurement Prioritization Based on Multi-Source Data Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Book collection is one of the important components in a library. Providing book collections is a challenge for libraries to ensure that these collections are in accordance with the needs of the user and the development of knowledge. To accomplish this, multi-source data integration is used, consisting of borrowing data, user suggestion data, and trend data. The results of the integration of multiple data sources in the form of keywords are implemented using the cosine similarity and BM25 methods to provide a list of book recommendations that are used as procurement priorities. Cosine similarity provides recommendations for 728 book titles and BM25 provides recommendations for 82 book titles. BM25 precision results get a value greater than cosine similarity which is 0.965, while the comparison of recall results cosine similarity is greater than BM25 which is 0.965. From the recommendation and comparison results, it can be concluded that cosine similarity provides a larger scope of book title recommendations than BM25 recommendations which are more selective. The larger scope of cosine similarity book title recommendation results allows the library to hold a more diverse collection and is appropriate for large libraries. While the more selective BM25 recommendation results can help with the procurement of focused collections, they are best suited for libraries with special collections.

articleTitle: Proposed Cargo Drone Model Respect to Actual Trajectory Tracking
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: A wide range of research continues to be conducted to improve the performance and efficiency of logistics drones. Most studies use simulation models to shorten test time and reduce test costs, but simulation results often have discrepancies with field test results. This paper presents an updated drone model to improve the compatibility of cargo drone simulation results with actual cargo drone flight test results in the field, especially in flight time compatibility. Euler equations of motion are simplified as the basis of the drone model to be developed. The variable added time was added from the linear regression results on the difference between the simulation results with the Euler equations of motion and the results of flight time in actual experiments in the field. The difference between the flight time of the cargo drone in the simulation using the proposed drone model and the flight time of the drone in the actual trial is less than 1 second when a 1-point flight test, a flight test with different weights, and a continuous flight test with three different flight scenarios are conducted.

articleTitle: Big Data Analytics of Green Stocks vs. Islamic Stocks: Are These Safe Havens?
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Green and Islamic stocks are alternative investment that provide investors with the option to build a diversified portfolio. This study explores the safe haven properties of Green stocks and Islamic stocks to shield wealth by using big data analytics. The data was gathered from selected Asia-Pacific countries, and the observation of this study was 8,488. Daily data was utilized from 6 December 2019 to 29 December 2023. To assess the big data analytics diversification benefits, we employed the method of moments quantile regression (MMQR) as the main methodology. The study shows that (1) Green stocks protect investors during uncertain times. (2) Islamic stocks can optimize the returns during different market conditions. (3) Green stocks provide better safe haven benefits than Islamic stocks during market turbulence. Investors need to understand not only the market sentiments but also the regulatory environment of the country before making an investment decision. This research provides information regarding investment strategies for investors, policymakers, and regulators.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of SBERT and FastText in Social Media Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Social media platforms such as Discord often create a number of hate speech content related to ethnicity, religion, race, and inter-group relations (SARA), posing challenges to user comfort and community harmony. This study investigates the effectiveness of SBERT and FastText embeddings in combination with Naive Bayes and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers for text classification tasks and the VADER method for sentiment analysis, using Indonesian-language Discord data. This work demonstrates that SVM outperforms Naive Bayes across all evaluation metrics, achieving higher AUC (86.3% vs. 79.3%), accuracy (83% vs. 71.8%), F1-Score (82.1% vs. 72.9%), Precision (82.8% vs. 79.1%), Recall (83% vs. 71.8%), and MCC (58.2% vs. 47.1%). The SVM outperforms high-dimensional data, and its robust margin-based decision making contributes to better performance in detecting SARA content. These findings underscore the importance of selecting appropriate embedding models and classifiers to optimize hate speech detection and sentiment analysis in informal and diverse linguistic contexts.

articleTitle: Impact of Reskilling initiatives on familiarity with AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study looks at how reskilling programs influence people's knowledge of artificial intelligence (AI). Rapid advancements in specialized fields during this time have increased interest in contributions connected to artificial intelligence for various organizations. As a result, businesses are launching reskilling initiatives to provide their staff with essential computer-based intelligence expertise. This study aims to assess how successfully these initiatives improve people's knowledge and skills related to concepts, tools, and applications of artificial intelligence. Through qualitative and quantitative research methods, such as surveys, focus groups, and contextual inquiries, the evaluation evaluates how reskilling initiatives aid participants in achieving man-made cognitive competency. This focus also looks at program design, delivery methods, teacher experience, and hierarchical support as factors that affect reskilling project outcomes. The judgments made by the Exploration should be observed by policymakers, educators, managers, and anyone attempting to investigate the rapidly evolving landscape of artificial intelligence-driven work settings and breakthroughs. Understanding how reskilling exercises affect simulated intelligence commonalities will finally help businesses create and manage more effective training programs to equip their employees for the future of man-made intelligence.

articleTitle: Developing a Scalable Next.js Platform for IoT Monitoring Using Backend-as-a-Service with a Comparison of Supabase and Firebase
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is progressing quickly in today’s interconnected world, where different gadgets and applications trade information consistently over the web. This ponder centers on creating an proficient IoT checking stage utilizing Next.js and a Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS) approach, with Firebase and Supabase as the essential arrangement alternatives. Leveraging Server-Side Rendering (SSR) and Static Site Generation (SSG) in Next.js enhances Search Engine Optimization (SEO) and by and large client encounter, supporting speedier and more responsive applications. Firebase and Supabase, with built-in real-time information synchronization, are fundamental for IoT’s energetic framework needs, guaranteeing information precision and fast upgrades. This inquire about compares the stages on execution, integration adaptability, and adaptability to decide the ideal choice for IoT checking. Discoveries demonstrate that Supabase, with its productive stack time and information administration, is superior suited for large-scale IoT applications, whereas Firebase’s robust integration capabilities and ease of use make it preferable for smaller, straightforward IoT projects.

articleTitle: Prediction Of Particulate Matter (PM) Concentration in Highland Wooden Houses Using XGBoost, LightGBM, And Catboost
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study aims to predict the concentration of PM2.5 within wooden houses located in highland areas using advanced machine learning models, namely CatBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM. These models are employed to analyze the impact of environmental factors, such as solar radiation temperature, wind speed, air temperature, humidity, and CO₂ concentration on indoor PM2.5 levels. The primary objective is to determine the model that provides the highest prediction accuracy, contributing to effective mitigation strategies for air quality management in similar environments. The findings demonstrate that the CatBoost model outperforms other models in terms of prediction accuracy, as evidenced by its lowest error metrics, including Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). In contrast, the stacking model, which combines all three algorithms, did not enhance prediction accuracy and exhibited higher error values in extreme cases compared to individual models. This research offers valuable insights into the application of boosting algorithms for indoor air quality prediction, especially in highland wooden structures. The results are expected to aid future developments in air quality monitoring systems and provide a foundation for targeted public health interventions.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Approach of Machine Learning Techniques for Forecasting on Small Dataset: A Case Study of City Waste
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In the context of increasingly complex waste management, predicting the emergence of waste is an important aspect of planning effective and sustainable management strategies. This research focuses on the challenges faced in predicting waste generation using small datasets, which often hinder the accuracy of forecasting models. We identified the main issue as the limitation of historical data, which can affect the model's ability to capture relevant patterns and trends. Therefore, the objective of this research is to explore the effectiveness of various machine learning techniques in generating accurate predictions for waste generation. The proposed method involves applying these models to processed historical datasets on waste generation to identify patterns and trends. Model performance evaluation is conducted using metrics commonly used in regression analysis, such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). Despite using a small dataset, the discussion of the results reveals that several machine learning models can provide good predictions, and selecting the right model is crucial to achieving high accuracy. The conclusion of this study confirms that, although there are challenges to using small datasets, the selection of the right model can produce accurate predictions for waste production. This study also provides recommendations for further research using larger datasets and more advanced techniques, emphasizing the importance of sustainable and efficient waste management. Thus, we expect this research to significantly contribute to the development of better and more responsive waste management strategies that meet the community's needs.

articleTitle: Internet of Things Attack Detection Based on K-Nearest Neighbor and Linear Discriminant Analysis Optimized with Chimpanzee Leader Election Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Along with the rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT), the threat to network security is also increasingly complex. IoT devices with limited computing capabilities make them a soft target for various cyber attacks. Therefore, an accurate, efficient, and lightweight attack detection system is needed to ensure the safety of IoT ecosystems. One promising approach is the use of a combination of machine learning techniques and optimization algorithms. This paper proposes the attack detection method on the IoT by combining the K-Nearest Neighbor (K-NN) classification method and the Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) optimized using the Chimpanzee Leader Election Optimization (CLEO) algorithm. This combined method can show excellent performance through experiments and testing using dataset IoT, which contains various types of attacks. The IoT attack detection results achieved classification accuracy above 85%, making it a competitive solution.

articleTitle: A Self-Adaptive Differential Artificial Bee Colony for Combined Economic Emission Dispatch of Power System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The energy sector heavily relies on fossil-fueled thermal power plants, significantly contributing to operational costs and greenhouse gas emissions. Optimizing these costs while reducing emissions remains a critical challenge in modern energy management. Dual-objective optimization methods are often complex due to their conflicting nature. This paper transforms the dual-objectives into a single-objective framework called Combined Economic Emission Dispatch (CEED) to address this issue. This study presents the self-adaptive differential artificial bee colony (sdABC) algorithm as a novel approach to addressing the CEED problem in power systems. The sdABC algorithm enhances the classical artificial bee colony (ABC) method by integrating differential evolution (DE) strategies and self-adaptive mechanisms. These advancements enable the algorithm to adapt dynamically to complex optimization landscapes, thereby ensuring accelerated convergence and improving the efficiency of solution space exploration. Simulations on the IEEE 30-bus test system were conducted to assess the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, considering transmission losses and operational constraints. The analysis confirms that the sdABC algorithm outperforms the classical ABC algorithm by achieving lower generation costs and reduced emissions.

articleTitle: The Effect of Feature Extraction Based on the Frequency of Emotionally Loaded Words using Part-of-Speech Tagging in Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Sentiment analysis plays a vital role in understanding public opinions. In this paper, we propose a methodology to improve sentiment classification models with features extracted using Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging. The feature extraction process involves building a vocabulary of frequently occurring words associated with specific parts of speech in both positive and negative sentiment datasets. These vocabularies are then used to calculate the frequency of occurrences in both training and testing datasets. We applied three traditional machine learning algorithms: Decision Tree, Random Forest, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) to evaluate the impact of these features. The dataset used in this study was collected from YouTube comments, focusing on public sentiment in Indonesia regarding the relocation of the capital city to Ibu Kota Nusantara (IKN). F1-score was used as the performance metric for evaluation. The experimental results demonstrated that models incorporating POS-tagged features showed improved performance compared to models without POS tagging. This suggests that POS tagging contributes to enhancing sentiment classification.

articleTitle: Leveraging FaceNet and SVM Hyperparameter Optimization in Face Recognition Attendance Systems with Limited Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Implementing a reliable Face Recognition Attendance System is crucial for organizations to streamline attendance tracking. Traditional methods, such as fingerprint and RFID systems, face significant limitations. Fingerprint systems can be hindered by factors such as moisture, injury, or environmental conditions, which affect their reliability. Similarly, RFID systems, while convenient for contactless entry, are susceptible to misuse, as cards may be used by individuals other than the registered users. This research overcomes these challenges by employing MTCNN for face detection, FaceNet for feature extraction, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classification, focusing on environments with limited data. The developed model achieved an impressive 100% accuracy on cross-validation training and independent test sets, showcasing its robustness even when operating under conditions of limited data. Hyperparameter tuning of the SVM led to the identification of optimal parameters, specifically C = 1 and gamma = 1, which resulted in the model consistently achieving a perfect 100% accuracy during cross-validation. Comparative analysis with ResNet50 and VGG16 highlighted the superiority of the FaceNet+SVM model, which demonstrated perfect classification results across all data. In contrast, ResNet50 and VGG16 exhibited signs of overfitting, failing to maintain accuracy on independent test data.

articleTitle: Weather Event Classification based on Microblog Data using Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Indonesia, which is located in the equatorial region with two seasons, the rainy and dry seasons, is challenging for weather forecasting because of significant changes in weather due to atmospheric disturbances. Previous experiments on weather event classification provided main class related to weather (sunny, cloudy, rainy and extreme). However, in these experiments, we attempted to include class "other", which is not related to inclass and weather events, to reflect the real-world dataset of natural language. From these experiments, the dataset from microblogs must be preprocessing, however not only common preprocessing namely stopwords and lowercase. It is important to determine which class has the lowest accuracy. Based on this experiment with 5 class data (sunny, cloudy, rainy, extreme and other), class "other" with the lowest accuracy was 0.71, and at the first stage preprocessing achieved an F1 Score of 0.839. Second stage preprocessing was conducted with the addition words "ibarat" or "like" and "prakiraan" or "forecast" and the performance model increased accuracy by 8% compared to before with an F1 Score of 0.917. The experiment continued to compare high epoch and small epoch, at small epoch at number of epoch is 2, result of F1 Score by 0.912. High epoch with 200 epochs and early stopping 20 increased accuracy by 0.5% than 2 epochs. Result from experiments, best performance to classify weather events achieved using indobenchmark/indobert-large-p2 with 200 epochs and early stopping 20 with accuracy of 91.7%, precision of 92.0%, recall of 91.7%, and F1 Score by 91.7%.

articleTitle: Water Quality Sensor Noise Classification based on Drone Movement using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Water pollution caused by human activities and environmental changes has become a critical issue. The challenges of directly analyzing water quality in remote or inaccessible aquatic environments highlight the importance of combining drones and water quality sensors. However, external factors, such as wind-induced drone movements, can introduce noise into sensor readings, compromising the accuracy of data collection. This study focuses on addressing the patterns of drone movements and their impact on sensor noise to enhance the reliability of water quality monitoring. In this research, experimental results demonstrate that machine learning models effectively analyzed the movement patterns, with detailed performance metrics for each algorithm. XGBoost (extreme gradient boosting), Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression were among the methods that were assessed. The Random Forest model outperformed the others, including XGBoost, Decision Tree, and Logistic Regression, with an accuracy of 97%, compared to 96% and 85%, respectively. The findings identify Random Forest as the most effective algorithm for analyzing movement patterns and mitigating noise in sensor data, thereby improving the overall reliability of water quality assessments.

articleTitle: Difference in Reaction and Accuracy between Visual Semantic Memory and Verbal Recognition Memory through Game-based Learning Understanding Javanese Language at the Elementary School Level
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study aims to explore the impact of Visual Semantic Memory and Verbal Recognition Memory approaches on student reactions and accuracy in game-based learning. The research employs a between-subjects experimental design, with one group receiving a visual approach and the other a verbal approach. Data were collected through in-game timer and data collection process was carried out for 30 to 45 minutes to evaluate student performance in answering time-based quizzes. Analysis was performed using non-parametric methods, with a Mann-Whitney test to assess significant differences between groups. The results revealed a significant difference in reaction times between VSM and VRM. The average reaction time for VSM was 8.82 seconds, while VRM had an average of 15.12 seconds, indicating faster information processing in VSM. However, the analysis of accuracy did not show a significant difference, suggesting that both VSM and VRM achieved comparable levels of accuracy in information recognition and processing. This is potential for accelerating student responses, contributing valuable insights to the development of more effective game-based learning, particularly in language education.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Statistical and Machine Learning Models for Price Prediction: A Case Study for Agricultural Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Traditional econometric models, such as the Fixed Effects Model (FEM) and Random Effects Model (REM), effectively address structured datasets by capturing fixed and inter-group variability but face limitations in handling non-linear relationships, multicollinearity, and temporal dynamics. This study evaluates the performance of FEM and REM against advanced machine learning (ML) models like XGBoost and CatBoost and deep learning (DL) models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), on agricultural panel datasets. Performance is assessed using metrics like Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Square Error (MSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). The results highlight FEM’s robustness for datasets with simpler or moderately complex structures, such as those associated with crops like Soya and Corn. However, ML models demonstrated better capacity to manage non-linearities, albeit requiring substantial feature engineering to leverage cross-sectional and temporal attributes. DL models showed promise in capturing temporal dependencies but faced challenges with cross-sectional heterogeneity. The study underscores the importance of aligning model selection with dataset characteristics. While FEM remains a reliable choice for panel data, ML and DL methods hold transformative potential when coupled with advanced architectures like hierarchical models or attention mechanisms. Future research could explore hybrid approaches that integrate statistical and advanced learning techniques to address the diverse complexities in agricultural datasets, paving the way for more accurate, scalable, and efficient predictive solutions in precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Forensic Image Enhancement and Forgery Detection Using Advanced Image Processing Techniques and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Nowadays, there is a wide use of modern techniques and technology in general, which constitutes an important innovation. Manipulating, changing and modifying digital images has become very popular and relatively easy, which has created a great challenge and concern, especially in cases that rely on digital images as the main evidence for issuing judgments. In order to improve the quality of images and accurately identify fraud cases, a talented system has been invented to conduct forensic investigations by combining modern image processing techniques and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). In this experiment, Google Colab was used as an experimental platform to apply a pixel-based approach to extract features from three separate experiments. An approach to forgery detection using pixel base algorithm was tested in relation to multiple conditions within separate experiments involving CNNs integration. Experiment1, which had a rudimentary CNN architecture, achieved an accuracy of 94.53% and validation accuracy of 94.54%. Experiment 2, with a sophisticated CNN structure, resulted in an accuracy of 94.91%, and a validation accuracy of 94.92%.

articleTitle: Voltammetry Data for Aquatic Pollutants Detection: A Comparative Study of Dimensionality Reduction Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Water pollution is an urgent environmental issue because it can have serious impacts on human health and the balance of ecosystems. The increase in industrial and agricultural activities has led to a rise in hazardous pollutants in water sources. One type of pollutant that has recently become a concern is heavy metals. Voltammetry methods have proven effective in detecting pollution, especially heavy metals in water. The data generated by voltammetry are complex and high-dimensional, necessitating procedures to reduce the dimensions. This research aims to find the best combination of dimensionality reduction techniques and classification methods. The dimensionality reduction techniques used are Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), AutoEncoder, and Independent Component Analysis (ICA). The classification methods implemented are Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression (LR), and Decision Tree (DT). The results of the study show that RF-PCA is the best combination, achieving an accuracy of 0.96.

articleTitle: Investigating the Causes of Flight Delays in the UAE Aviation: A Quantitative Study on IATA-Coded Delay Subcategories
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The paper investigates the causes of flight delays in the UAE aviation industry and focusing on participants' perceptions to identify areas for operational improvements. This research study addresses flight delays in the UAE aviation industry and focusing on key operational causes and their implications. The study utilized structured survey with 52 respondents consisting of pilots, maintenance staff, and customer service representatives to analyze delay factors. The analysis included descriptive statistics, and Chi-square test for independence to determine the significance of associations between each delay cause and respondents' agreement levels. Results emphasized that technical problems and handling challenges are impactful, with a portion of participants perceiving these as significant contributors to delays. Weather conditions and air traffic control-related issues were also identified as influential, and though less so than technical and handling factors. Results highlight air traffic control-related issues (51%), passenger/baggage issues (36%), and technical problems (38%) are significant contributors to flight delays, while weather conditions also showing impact operations (42%). Neutral responses for miscellaneous causes (36%) indicate mixed perceptions. The findings emphasize on the need for better air traffic management, streamlined passenger handling, and enhanced technical reliability. The Chi-square test result at a value of 0.636, suggests no strong evidence of dependency between the delay factors and participants’ perceptions, and indicating independent causes without significant overlap in participants’ views. The analysis and findings point to a need for targeted interventions to enhance operational efficiency focus on baggage handling, technical maintenance, and air traffic management improvements. The addressing of these major areas, the UAE aviation industry enhance passenger satisfaction, better mitigate delays, and streamline operations. The identification of critical delay factors, this research study contributes actionable insights for industry stakeholders to improve operational efficiency and reduce disruptions in the UAE aviation sector.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling with XGBoost for Optimizing Moodle’s Distributed E-Learning Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study examines the impact of user activity on the performance of Moodle's distributed infrastructure at Universitas Pelita Harapan (UPH) and evaluates the role of predictive modeling in optimizing server specifications. By analyzing server log data from web servers, database servers, and Redis cache, this research identifies correlations between concurrent users and resource utilization metrics, such as CPU and memory usage. Results indicate a low to moderate positive correlation between user load and CPU usage, while memory usage shows a stronger dependency on user activity in specific components, such as web servers. Predictive models were developed using XGBoost to forecast CPU and memory demands. The results show high accuracy, with R-square values reaching up to 1.00. These models enable dynamic resource scaling, ensuring system stability and cost efficiency during peak loads. The findings provide actionable insights for optimizing Moodle’s distributed infrastructure, supporting scalable resource management, and enhancing e-learning platform performance under variable user loads.

articleTitle: Classification of Natural Disaster Messages in Social Media using 3D input with 2D/3D CNN BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Natural disasters such as floods, earthquakes, and forest fires pose global threats that require swift and accurate responses to minimize losses. This study proposes a novel approach to classifying disaster-related information from social media posts by integrating data from Indonesian Twitter and Wikipedia. By employing advanced word embedding techniques (Word2Vec, FastText, and GloVe) alongside hybrid deep learning architectures (2D CNN Bi-LSTM and 3D CNN BiLSTM), this research enhances feature representation and model performance. Evaluation results demonstrate that the 2D CNN Bi-LSTM Type 2 achieves the highest accuracy for classifying floods (86.05%) and earthquakes (86.00%), while the 3D CNN Bi-LSTM Type 2 excels in classifying forest fires (86.11%). These findings highlight the model's ability to effectively extract spatial and temporal patterns, supporting improved disaster message classification performance. Nevertheless, challenges remain in maintaining consistent performance across all disaster categories. Future research could focus on optimizing data representation and architectural adaptability for further advancements.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Driven Nutrition Facts Traceability in Indonesia: Enhancing Transparency and Trust in the Food Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Indonesia faces significant challenges in ensuring transparency and accuracy in nutrition labeling, particularly due to the prevalence of unverified claims in the market. To address these issues, the integration of blockchain technology into nutrition facts and Certificate of Analysis (CoA) traceability presents a transformative solution for enhancing This study introduces two blockchain-based models designed to meet distinct objectives: the first focuses on enhancing consumer traceability of BPOM (Badan Pengawas Obat dan Makanan or Indonesian Food and Drug Authority) licenses, while the second targets CoA traceability to ensure batch-specific quality consistency. Embedding these processes in a decentralized system allows stakeholders to verify nutrition facts and quality claims through immutable and transparent records. Smart contracts automate critical functions, such as regulatory audits, license issuance, and CoA validation, ensuring data integrity and streamlining compliance processes. Internal traceability offers stakeholders detailed insights into production and distribution, while external traceability empowers consumers with comprehensive product information through a single QR code scan. These findings highlight the research's significant contributions by proposing blockchain models designed specifically for nutrition facts and CoA traceability, addressing key gaps in traditional food labeling systems. These models ensure immutable records and enable seamless verification processes. This research aligns with objectives to enhance consumer trust, improve regulatory compliance, and support business valuation by creating a transparent, efficient system that empowers both stakeholders and consumers.

articleTitle: Predicting Birth Rates Using Random Forest, Long Short-Term Memory and Exponential Smoothing: A Study on Kotawaringin Barat Regency, Central Kalimantan, Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Predicting birth rates accurately is essential for effective population planning. Traditional time series methods like Exponential Smoothing have been applied to birth rate forecasting but often fail to achieve high accuracy. This work suggests a novel approach using advanced machine learning, notably Random Forest (RF) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), to predict birth rates in Kotawaringin Barat Regency, Central Kalimantan Province, Indonesia, using daily birth records from 2015 to 2023. The contribution of this study lies in evaluating the performance of these methods against Exponential Smoothing to determine which model is the most successful for this context. From the evaluation, this research predicts birth rates with Exponential Smoothing and LSTM models resulting in MAPE values of 0.32 and 0.38 and the lowest error, achieving 0.09 MAPE using the Random Forest method.

articleTitle: Automated Lung Disease Classification Using YOLOv8 Based on Chest X-Ray Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Pneumonia remains a critical global health challenge, particularly affecting children, with the World Health Organization reporting 740,180 child deaths in 2019. This study introduces an innovative approach to lung disease classification using YOLOv8, a state-of-the-art deep learning architecture, to automatically detect and differentiate between normal lung conditions, viral pneumonia, and COVID-19 using chest X-ray images. The research employs a comprehensive dataset of 312 chest X-ray images, categorized into three distinct classes: COVID-19 (132 images), Viral Pneumonia (90 images), and Normal (90 images). Utilizing the YOLOv8-cls variant with transfer learning techniques pre-trained on ImageNet, we evaluated model performance using multiple evaluation metrics: Precision (100%), indicating zero false positive prediction, Recall (94.78%), demonstrating high sensitivity in disease detection, F1-Score (97.32%) and Top-1 Accuracy (94.8%), with class-specific accuracies of COVID-19 (100%), Normal lung conditions (90%), and Viral Pneumonia (86%) reflecting a balanced performance between precision and recall. Comparative benchmarking against existing methodologies, including Convolutional Neural Networks (91.54% accuracy) and K-Nearest Neighbor algorithms (63% accuracy), underscores the proposed YOLOv8-based approach's superior performance. The study addresses critical research limitations by offering a larger, more diverse dataset, comprehensive computational efficiency metrics, and expanded classification complexity. The proposed model maintains high accuracy while ensuring real-time processing capabilities, presenting a promising solution for automated, rapid lung disease screening in clinical settings. Future research will focus on optimizing model speed, sensitivity, computational efficiency, and expanding the image dataset to enhance model inclusivity and robustness.

articleTitle: Implementation of Machine Learning Algorithm for Stroke Risk Classification by Applying Sequential Forward Selection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Stroke is a critical medical condition that can abruptly impair brain function. It may arise from either hemorrhaging or obstruction within the blood vessels. Stroke ranks as the second most common cause of death worldwide and is the third primary contributor to disability. This study employs machine learning methodologies, including Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and LightGBM, to assess the classification of stroke risk. The classification is conducted in two phases: first without feature selection and then utilizing Sequential Forward Selection (SFS) for feature selection. Findings indicate that implementing SFS with an 80:20 data-sharing ratio enhances classification accuracy compared to the approach without feature selection. SFS identifies nine key features: gender, age, hypertension, smoking status, BMI, average glucose level, marital status, employment type, and residence type. Utilizing these nine features achieved the highest accuracy of 95.94%, with a recall of 95.77%, precision of 96.07%, F1-Score of 95.92%, and AUC of 99.32%, outperforming both the Random Forest and LightGBM algorithms. These results demonstrate that the model effectively classifies stroke risk data by focusing on pertinent features.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization for Disaster Evacuation using NSGA-II: A Case Study in Parangtritis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Parangtritis, a popular tourist destination on the southern coast of Java, faces a high tsunami risk due to tectonic activity along nearby subduction zones. The main challenges in this area include a large number of tourists, vulnerable populations such as the elderly and disabled, and limited shelter capacity, which can lead to congestion during evacuation. To address these issues, this study proposes a multi-objective approach using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to support efficient and adaptive evacuation planning. The model optimizes five objective functions: evacuation distance, evacuation time, shelter capacity, congestion costs, and shelter distribution variance, while conducting sensitivity analysis to ensure solution stability. The implementation results show that NSGA-II effectively generates high-quality Pareto fronts, validated using hypervolume and Generational Distance (GD) metrics, and highlights trade-offs between evacuation objectives, offering data-driven insights for designing more efficient evacuation strategies in Parangtritis.

articleTitle: Rating Expectations Based Analysis for Predicting Hotel Review Sentiment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This research explores the integration of expectation-based sentiment analysis to improve the accuracy of sentiment predictions using a hotel review dataset sourced from Kaggle. The analysis leverages Python and Incorporates advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) tools, including HuggingFace Transformers for the RoBERTa model and Keras for the LSTM model. Data visualization is performed with Matplotlib and seaborn to identify trends, while preprocessing steps such as tokenization ensure the dataset is optimally structured for model training, Unlike earlier works, this study introduces the use of weighted expectation scores derived from hotel ratings, providing an enriched contextual layer to sentiment analysis. RoBERTa facilitates tokenization. capturing semantic nuances, while LSTM is employed to model sequential dependencies in textual data. A robust evaluation process involving 5-fold Cross Validation is employed, with performance assessed through metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Mean Squared Error (MSE). Results Indicate that combining ROBERT, LSTM, and expectation scores yields an accuracy of 93% MAE and an MSE of of 1.5581. This novel approach offers valuable insights into customer sentiment by incorporating their expectations, paving the way for more informed and effective sentiment analysis techniques.

articleTitle: Prototyping Network-connected Multi-sensor Node of Wearable Device for Inpatient Monitoring System: Sensor Calibration Aspect
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
