abstract: Inpatient room monitoring system has its prominence in fulfilling a smart hospital system in healthcare industry. Monitoring patient itself has its importance such as monitoring the patient who is in intensive care unit or in isolated inpatient room. It requires a real-time monitoring system that can observe patient conditions. Therefore, it is necessary to realize a real-time patient monitoring system through a wearable device. It is as our long-term goal to realize network-based wearable device for such inpatient monitoring system. Motivated by such long-term goal, this paper presents calibration aspects for prototyping a network-connected wearable device in which the device is based on muti-sensor node. Each sensor certainly requires a good accuracy value or level before being used commercially or applied to the patients. Therefore, calibration is needed. The calibrated sensors are the MAX30100 sensor as the patient's pulse and oxygen respiration sensor and the DS18B20 sensor as the patient's body temperature sensor. The method used in this calibration uses the linear regression since the two sensors have a simple and consistent relationship between the sensor output and the measured value from a standard measurement tool. The calibrated sensors are then validated using Bland Altman plot. The results have good accuracies with all parameters have more than 99% of accuracy. Multi-sensor device can be implemented as a prototype of wearable device for real-time inpatient room monitoring system.

articleTitle: Regional Clustering for Stunting Prevalence Analysis in Central Java Using Possibilistic Fuzzy C-Means (PFCM) Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Stunting is a condition in toddler where their growth is impaired, resulting in a height significantly below what is considered normal for their age. Indonesia has a notably high prevalence of stunting, reaching 24.4% in 2021. Central Java is one of the provinces that became a central government focus in accelerating the reduction of stunting prevalence. Several factors contribute to the high prevalence of stunting in Central Java, including inadequate nutrition for children and pregnant women resulting in low birth weight, insufficient exclusive breastfeeding, a high rate of early marriages, limited access to sanitation and clean water sources, and the economic inability of families to meet the nutritional needs of mothers and children. This requires regional mapping based on stunting variables to create targeted policies. This study examines the grouping of districts/cities in Central Java Province using the Possibilistic Fuzzy C-Means (PFCM) algorithm. A fuzzy silhouette coefficient is used to identify an optimal number of clusters. Application of this method demonstrates that the districts/cities within this province can be clustered into five groups.

articleTitle: Simulation Study and Application to Compare the Performance of the K-Means and K-Medoids Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The research compared k-means and k-medoids clustering algorithms using simulated datasets. The k-means divides data into several clusters using the average value as the cluster center (centroid), while the k-medoids uses medoids as the cluster center. The performance of these two methods is compared using simulation studies that consider factors such as the number of clusters, population size, data dimensionality, and geometric shape. Simulation studies provide information about which data characteristics are most suitable for clustering using the k-means and k-medoids. K-medoids generally outperform k-means in clustering accuracy across various factors. This is particularly evident in scenarios with more clusters, larger populations, and non-spherical data distributions. However, k-means may be more suitable for smaller datasets with fewer clusters and more spherical data. For the real application, the data used is the Indonesian Democracy Index Aspect for the year 2022. After considering data characteristics, it was determined that the k-medoids is more appropriate for analysis of this real dataset than the k-means, particularly for scenarios with multiple clusters, larger populations, and non-spherical data distributions.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Approach for Sentiment Analysis of GoFood Services
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In the age of swift digital advancement, social media has emerged as a vital and readily available information source for users. Individuals utilize social media to communicate, articulate thoughts, and disseminate their viewpoints, both textually and visually. Twitter is a social media platform that people extensively utilize to disseminate both favorable and unfavorable information regarding GoFood services. This study intends to apply the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) algorithm within the GoFood service on Twitter. This research also seeks to assess the accuracy of the CNN algorithm in relation to GoFood services. Employing deep learning techniques, particularly the convolutional neural network algorithm, to analyze Twitter user sentiment can enhance the efficiency, accuracy, and simplicity of classifying answers to GoFood services. The findings indicated that the Convolutional Neural Network technique was effectively employed to classify positive, negative, and neutral feelings. The optimal accuracy rate was attained through preprocessing with Stemming, yielding 51% accuracy for multiclass classification and 72% for binary class classification. The accuracy percentage for classification without stemming was 49% for multiclass classification and 70% for binary classification. This research holds possible consequences for Gojek firms and can serve as evaluative and assessment material for GoFood services, enabling them to implement necessary corrective measures.

articleTitle: Effect of Anterior Commisure - Posterior Commisure Reorientation for 3D Aneurysm Segmentation in the Brain
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study explores the effect of Anterior Commissure - Posterior Commissure (AC-PC) reorientation on 3D aneurysm segmentation accuracy in brain MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) using the UNetR (UNet with Transformers) model. Accurate segmentation is critical in diagnosing life-threatening conditions like hemorrhagic stroke from aneurysm rupture. Given the importance of consistent imaging, AC-PC landmarks serve as valuable reference points for enhancing alignment. We conducted two preprocessing experiments: (1) reshaped to (256, 256, 256), and (2) reshaped to (256, 256, 256) with rotation based on the AC-PC line. Each experiment was evaluated by Dice score coefficient, yielding average scores of 0.22 (SD=0.19), and 0.24 (SD=0.21), respectively. While a paired t-test showed no statistically significant effect from AC-PC reorientation, the rotated data produced an approximate 9.4% improvement in segmentation accuracy. These findings suggest that incorporating AC-PC alignment may contribute to more reliable aneurysm segmentation in brain MRI, supporting the broader use of spatial reorientation to enhance diagnostic accuracy in AI-driven medical imaging

articleTitle: Soulbot: Chatbots for Mental Health Support using Gemini
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Mental health is becoming an increasingly important concern, especially after the COVID-19 pandemic. Cases of suicide due to stress, depression, mental illness, academic pressure, and lack of communication are increasing in Generation Z. So, as a preventive measure and handling mental health, intense communication is needed. This research aims to develop an Indonesian-language chatbot called "Soulbot" to help Generation Z overcome their anxiety and depression by providing information or responding as needed by utilizing Generative AI technology and Architecture Transformers. Soulbot is designed using the Gemini algorithm, which can generate realistic text and understand context so that the chatbot can provide relevant and useful responses for users. In addition, this method is also used to study data to improve the quality of interaction and user experience. The results of the study show that Soulbot is able to provide the right response in the context of mental health. The evaluation using Semantics Cosine Similarity resulted in an average score of 84%, with the highest score reaching 95%. Based on the evaluation, Soulbot showed a good ability to understand and respond to mental health-related questions with varying degrees of similarity. With this chatbot, it is hoped that public awareness will increase about the importance of maintaining mental health among students, both in the world of education and in the family environment.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter Optimization of 2D CNN LSTM for Natural Disaster Classification from Social Media Messages
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Social media plays a crucial role in providing information related to natural disasters, which can help accelerate the response to such events. Messages shared by social media users can offer valuable insights into natural disaster occurrences. The use of a 2D CNN model combined with LSTM has been applied in previous research for classifying natural disasters. Word embedding techniques such as Word2Vec, FastText, and GloVe have been utilized, but there are still limitations in the word representations used. This research aims to address these shortcomings by incorporating wikipedia text into the word embedding process, which is expected to enhance word representations. Additionally, the research also applies hyperparameter tuning using a grid search method to optimize the performance of the 2D CNN + LSTM model. The results obtained from this research show improved accuracy compared to previous research, with accuracy values reaching 83.55% for floods, 92.11% for forest fires, and 81.83% for earthquakes. These findings demonstrate that the inclusion of wikipedia text in word embedding and the optimization of the 2D CNN + LSTM model through hyperparameter tuning with grid search significantly improve the model’s accuracy.

articleTitle: Analyzing STEM Women’s Employability: A Machine Learning Framework with Clustering and Multi-Target Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The gender gap in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) fields highlights significant research opportunities, particularly in examining the employability of female graduates. This study introduces a novel machine learning framework integrating Clustering and Multi-target Classification to analyze employment waiting time and job linearity among women STEM alumni. Using K-Means Clustering and Multi-Target Logistic Regression, the framework achieved a classification accuracy of 77% and a silhouette score of 0.61, demonstrating its effectiveness in predictive analysis. Beyond these results, the framework offers a robust methodology for integrating Clustering with Classification, enabling a nuanced understanding of the employability challenges faced by women in STEM. This approach identifies key patterns in employment data, paving the way for targeted interventions and actionable insights. Furthermore, the findings aim to inform data-driven policymaking and future research to improve employability outcomes. This work contributes to addressing systemic challenges and fostering gender diversity in STEM careers while enhancing opportunities for women.

articleTitle: Influence of Text-Based Chatbot, Privacy Concern, and Trust Mediation in the Usage Continuance of Chatbots in E-Commerce
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: User experience has been greatly impacted by the rapid growth of artificial intelligence in e-commerce, particularly through the use of text-based chatbots. These chatbots, while offering benefits such as instant response, cost-effectiveness, and personalized assistance, face challenges related to user perceptions and trust. This study explores the challenges in adopting text-based chatbots in e-commerce, particularly from a user experience (UX) perspective, using the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) framework. A quantitative methodology was employed, surveying Indonesian e-commerce users who interact with chatbots. The study tested six hypotheses, revealing that empathy and friendliness positively influence trust, while credibility, anthropomorphism, and privacy concerns do not significantly impact trust. Trust, in turn, was found to be a critical determinant of users' continued use of chatbots. These findings underscore the importance of enhancing chatbot features to better meet user needs, suggesting that improving empathy, friendliness, and contextual adaptation could lead to more trustworthy and engaging user experiences. This study overall provides insights for developers and e-commerce practitioners to design more effective chatbots that not only meet functional needs but also strengthen the overall user experience.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis on Spectrum Utilization Efficiency of 1900 MHz for 5G-Railways: A Case Study for Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The rail industry is transitioning from the Global System for Mobile Communications-Railway (GSM-R) to the Future Railway Mobile Communications System (FRMCS). Using advanced fifth-generation (5G) technology, FRMCS addresses the limitations of GSM-R and meets the requirements of modern railways. In this paper, we select the island of Java, which has the longest railway track in Indonesia, as the research area. We analyze the performance on spectrum utilization efficiency (SUE) of 1900 MHz for 5G-Railway in Indonesia. We determine the maximum allowable path loss (MAPL) to calculate the required number of base stations and evaluate the feasibility of investment considering the current business conditions of railway operators. We found that the efficiency of spectrum utilization increases as the physical size of the cell and the cluster size decreases. We also found that utilizing the 1900 MHz spectrum as a class license yields higher Net Present Value (NPV) and Internal Rate of Return (IRR) values, along with a shorter payback period. The results of this paper are expected to offer a reference for implementing FRMCS in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Detecting Phising Website using Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Modern phishing is a sophisticated cyberattack. It steals login details and payment information by posing as a trusted entity. With our increasing dependence on digital platforms, the frequency and sophistication of phishing attacks have escalated. Many studies have examined phishing detection. Most prioritize metrics like accuracy, precision, and recall. However, a significant research gap exists as previous studies have primarily focused on accuracy and evaluation metrics without incorporating validation processes to verify whether the developed models are adequately robust and reliable. Harnessing the power of machine learning, we can classify websites into authentic or fraudulent categories, proposing a robust defense against these malicious schemes. The purpose of this study is to present the novelty of a concise summary of techniques for detecting phishing and to create a framework that can be used to detect phishing. The dataset comprises 662,590 entries and 9 features. This study implements three supervised learning models: Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and XGBoost algorithms. These algorithms were chosen for their dataset knowledge and applicability. According to experiments, the Decision Tree model has the lowest accuracy at 88.66% and the KNN model the highest at 88.94%. The XGBoost model records an accuracy of 90.24%. XGBoost often achieves high accuracy due to its gradient boosting framework, which combines multiple decision trees to minimize errors. Its regularization techniques also help prevent overfitting, leading to robust performance on unseen data.

articleTitle: Comparison of Random Search and Grid Search for Optimizing SVM in Stroke Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study examines the application of machine learning for stroke disease classification, emphasizing the need for precise model optimization to enhance predictive accuracy. The research focuses on the performance of the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm, comparing two hyperparameter tuning approaches: Random Search and Grid Search. The methodology includes stages of Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), Data Preprocessing, Classification Modeling, Performance Evaluation, and Hyperparameter Tuning using a stroke classification dataset. Results reveal that SVM optimized with Random Search achieved an accuracy of 90.44%, outperforming the Grid Search method. These findings highlight the significance of effective data preprocessing and model optimization in developing reliable predictions and advancing strategies for better stroke prevention and management. The study demonstrates the pivotal role of machine learning in early stroke detection and risk assessment, providing insights into practical applications for healthcare. The results establish that random search is preferred for improving SVM performance in critical diagnostic tasks.

articleTitle: Utilizing Large Language Models (LLM) for Optimizing Faculty Schedule Communication through Google Calendar Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study presents the development of a Large Language Model (LLM)-based system, specifically LLaMA 3.2 11B, to optimize schedule communication in higher education institutions through integration with the Google Calendar API. The system is designed to understand natural language inputs, detect schedule conflicts, and provide adaptive solutions in real-time. Leveraging advanced LLM capabilities, the system effectively handles ambiguous and multilingual inputs while ensuring contextual accuracy. A dataset of 1,000 entries simulating academic schedules was utilized, including 50% ambiguous queries and 20% multilingual cases, reflecting diverse real-world scenarios. Comparative benchmarks with rule-based and classical machine learning models demonstrate the superiority of the LLM-based approach, achieving a conflict detection accuracy of 96%, latency of 6 seconds, and user satisfaction score of 4.6 out of 5. These results outperform rule-based (84% accuracy, 11 seconds latency) and classical ML systems (90% accuracy, 9 seconds latency). The findings highlight the system’s ability to dynamically adapt to user preferences and real-time scheduling challenges, offering significant efficiency improvements and user-centric interactions. This research contributes to the advancement of AI in digital scheduling systems, emphasizing scalability and applicability in multilingual, high-load environments. Future work includes expanding datasets, enhancing NLP for ambiguous inputs, and integrating cross-time-zone scheduling capabilities.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Maturity Level of SMEs in Indonesia in The Greater Jakarta Area
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence Technology is currently developing so widely in many industries. In the Small and Medium Enterprises or SMEs industry, the use of artificial intelligence can help optimize the productivity and efficiency of company operations. However, in Indonesia, the entrepreneur's readiness to use artificial intelligence still needs to be researched. This study aims to determine what factors can optimize AI adoption performance by using the TOE framework to get a comprehensive overview and discover how mature SMEs in Greater Jakarta area are in using AI. This study is supported by quantitative research methods, which prove the relationship between variables of each hypothesis. Data collection samples will be taken by distributing questionnaires through the Google Form platform. There are 5 variables tested in this study, namely Technology Readiness, Organizational Readiness, Environmental Readiness, AI Adoption, and Business Performance. Through this research, the result showed that technological and environmental readiness significantly influenced AI adoption which positively affected business performance. This research is expected to provide new literature regarding the evaluation of the maturity level for adopting artificial intelligence in SME businesses to effectively and efficiently improve and enhance SME business performance in adopting artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Exploring Millennial Security Awareness of Data Protection, Cybercrime, and Privacy Management in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Personal data is currently one of the most crucial things that should not be spread haphazardly to avoid cybercrime. Latest report from The International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL) in 2024 stated that Southeast Asia was the target of cybercriminals who tried to infect networks and devices through phishing tricks, in form of online scam as well as business mail scam. Indonesia was the highest target during the first half of 2019 with 31.07% of phishing attempts. This study examines and analyzes the effect of information security awareness on personal data protection, cybercrime, and communication privacy management. The research method used is descriptive analysis and data analysis using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) using Partial Least Squares (PLS). The results of this study indicate that information security awareness affects cybercrime. The millennial generation is aware that personal data are essential to protect, but they have not fully protected their data, thus cybercrime continues to increase. Meanwhile, information security awareness of personal data protection and communication privacy management do not affect each other.

articleTitle: Expert System for Early Detection of Kidney Disease Through E-Health Using Android-Based Dempster Shafer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The Ministry of Health (Kemenkes RI) discovered that more than 700 thousand Indonesians suffer from chronic kidney failure. According to data from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) Global Burden of Disease (GBD) in 2019, chronic kidney disease is among the top 10 diseases with the highest mortality in Indonesia . This study developed an Android-based expert system for early detection of kidney disease through an E-Health approach by implementing the Dempster Shafer algorithm. The purpose of this study is to design an application to help people in carrying out early detection of kidney disease independently based on the symptoms they experience. The methodology used includes data collection through literature studies and interviews with nephrology experts, as well as the implementation of the Dempster Shafer algorithm to calculate the level of confidence in the diagnosis based on a combination of symptoms inputted by the user. The test results show that the system has an accuracy level of 85% in detecting kidney disease based on validation by experts. This system successfully identifies various types of kidney diseases such as acute kidney failure, chronic kidney failure, kidney stones, and kidney infections with a reliable level of confidence. The implementation of the system in the form of an Android mobile application provides easy access for users to perform early detection of kidney disease anytime and anywhere. This research is expected to contribute to preventive efforts against kidney disease through the use of mobile-based expert system technology.

articleTitle: Optimizing Diabetes Diagnosis Using Machine Learning With SMOTE and Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study explores the use of machine learning for diabetes categorization, aiming to enhance diagnostic accuracy. Three classification algorithms—Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Decision Tree—are evaluated, with Random Forest achieving the highest accuracy of 97.53%, outperforming the others. To address class imbalance, the research employs the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), improving the model's ability to detect minority class instances. Feature selection is also implemented to optimize model performance. The methodology follows a structured approach, including Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA), Data Preprocessing, Model Classification, and Performance Evaluation. The findings highlight the importance of selecting appropriate techniques to improve the precision and reliability of diabetes diagnosis. By incorporating SMOTE and feature selection, the study demonstrates significant improvements in the accuracy and efficiency of diabetes diagnostic systems, potentially leading to better health outcomes. These results emphasize the value of integrating advanced machine learning methods in healthcare for more effective disease detection and management.

articleTitle: GAN-Driven Iterative Method for Automated IoT Intrusion Detection Architecture Design and Scalable Training-Set Creation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In this study, we propose an innovative iterative methodology employing Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to achieve two primary objectives: (i) develop a comprehensive knowledge base termed TAG (Training-set for Architecture Generation) to facilitate the automated training of GANs for creating architecture configurations of Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) without manual intervention, and (ii) utilize the iterative framework with TAG to derive optimal deep learning-based intrusion classifier architecture. Our proposed method overcomes the limitations inherent in traditional Neural Architecture Search (NAS), which is often restricted by a predefined search space and incurs high computational overhead. To the best of our knowledge, this study represents the first effort to create a dedicated knowledge base for training GANs, which serves as a training dataset to produce NIDS architecture configurations. The proposed approach not only enhances the efficiency of generating NIDS configurations by reducing computational costs and accelerating convergence but also introduces a novel strategy for developing a structured knowledge base to direct GAN training. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that employing TAG to guide GAN training results in the generation of deep learning-based intrusion classifier architecture with a reported accuracy of 99%, an optimal False Alarm Rate (FAR) of 0.01, precision of 97%, and recall of 99%.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning Models to Combat Fake News: A Study on RNN, CNN, and BERT Accuracy in Identifying Misinformation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Technological developments, especially in the last three decades, have greatly improved the ways in which the public gets information. These have made it possible to have relatively uncharted opportunities for extending one’s knowledge base without necessarily having to consult with others or update through physical media. However, access to news across websites, applications, and social media networks has increased equally in tandem and has increased opportunities for producing and sharing fake news. This research focuses on identifying the effect of deep learning models comprising RNN, CNN, and Transformer-based BERT in the fake news detection and classification problem. The dataset used is 76,537 samples, approximately an equal number of real and fake news and mostly in English. This means that CNN training yielded 96.15% accuracy while observing that RNN yielded 95.70%. Additionally, the Transformer-based BERT model performed even better, with an accuracy of 97.44 % better than the two with its bidirectional context comprehension. In order to comprehensively assess the model, such parameters used for evaluation as precision, recall, and F1-score were integrated into the model. This work also investigates the practical scenario of using such models in complex big-data applications and the problems associated with scalability, delay, and resource consumption. With the help of these superior models, this work helps minimize the effects of fake news and raise awareness in the realm of social media and the consumption of news.

articleTitle: Meta-Classifier Approach to Facial Expression Recognition Using DWT-Based Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Facial Expression Recognition (FER) is an important topic in image processing with several applications, including sentiment analysis, human-machine interaction, and security systems. This paper presents a meta-classifier strategy based on a Meta-Classifier ensemble approach that enhances facial expression recognition accuracy by leveraging the features derived from Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) extraction. The meta-classifier combines predictions from multiple machine learning models, such as K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree (DT), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), to optimize classification performance by exploiting the complementary strengths of each model. The experiment's results show that the meta-classifier outperforms individual models by 94.06% accuracy, 94.06% precision, 93.91% recall, and 94.33% F1-Score. Furthermore, confusion matrix analysis emphasizes the model's capacity to accurately categorize numerous facial expressions, demonstrating its resilience and dependability. This methodology highlights the superiority of a meta-classifier approach over individual classifiers, providing a solid basis for handling FER issues such as uneven lighting, varying facial angles, and complicated expressions. The suggested technique represents a substantial step forward in the development of FER-based systems, enabling more efficient and accurate emotion detection for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Paradox: Empowering Cyber Defense with Artificial Intelligence in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), which helps people with a variety of tasks, from easy to difficult, has become an essential part of everyday life. Data abnormalities in Indonesia grew dramatically in 2023, indicating a higher cybersecurity risk. This paper discusses the challenge of utilizing AI to improve cybersecurity while also recognizing some of its possible disadvantages. Although AI's ability to identify threats quickly, the low adoption rate of AI-driven cybersecurity solutions in Indonesia is still concerning considering the low adoption rate. This study highlights a substantial lack of understanding about the factors influencing people's intentions to use AI-based cybersecurity solutions in their workplaces. We used a quantitative method by a questionnaire that consisted of 42 questions using a Likert scale varying from 1 (strongly disagree) to 6 (strongly agree) to gather data on individuals who works across a variety of Indonesian businesses and employment positions in order to thoroughly understand this gap. The study looks at a variety of key variables that affect AI-based cybersecurity tools adoption intentions, such as perceived self-efficacy, job insecurity, perceived vulnerability, perceived severity, perceived self-efficacy, facilitating conditions, and resistance to change. For data analysis, the study makes use of Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), with Smart PLS serving as the primary statistical tool. This study aims to provide business leaders and AI developers beneficial understanding by identifying these elements and the variables that drive them. With this, the study hopes that the results will guide the creation and distribution of efficient cybersecurity solutions that ease customer worries and increase adoption rates. The ultimate goal of this research is to strengthen defence against new attacks and lower cybersecurity risks in Indonesia by utilizing AI-based cybersecurity tools.

articleTitle: Forecasting Electricity Demand at PLN ULP Cipanas Using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Accurate electricity demand forecasting is essential to maintaining grid stability and operational efficiency, especially in regions like the Perusahaan Listrik Negara (PLN) Unit Layanan Pelanggan (ULP) Cipanas, where demand fluctuations are influenced by external factors such as daily temperatures and tourism activities during holidays. Traditional methods like Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) often fail to capture the non-linear patterns and complex long-term dependencies in time-series data. This study introduces an innovative approach by integrating historical electricity demand data with external variables, such as daily temperatures and day type information (workdays or holidays), using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). The integration of these variables significantly enhances the model’s performance, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 21.89 Amperes, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 28.79 Amperes, and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 5.01%. The inclusion of temperature and day type variables helps the model capture seasonal fluctuations and demand spikes, particularly during holidays and weekends, which are unique to Cipanas as a tourist destination. This approach not only overcomes the limitations of traditional methods but also offers a more effective solution for managing the complexities of electricity demand forecasting in regions with dynamic external influences.

articleTitle: Optimization of Gas Sensor Array in Electronic Nose Using Whale Optimization Algorithm for Tuberculosis Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: A lung infected with tuberculosis contains volatile organic compounds (VOCs) caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. An exhaled breath analysis approach can detect biomarkers of tuberculosis. An electronic nose can be proposed as a device for the early diagnosis of tuberculosis. The primary problem with this device is to specify the optimal number of gas sensors while maintaining high performance. The whale optimization algorithm (WOA) is an optimization method that uses the hunting mechanism of humpback whales, including bubble-net feeding and spiral movement. This algorithm is straightforward to implement, uncomplicated, and converges quickly. This study aimed to determine the optimal number of gas sensors in an electronic nose for differentiating between patients with tuberculosis and healthy controls through exhaled breath using WOA. The implementation was performed using Python programming and Jupyter Notebook for data processing, optimization, and classification. The experimental results demonstrate that the WOA efficiently selected the optimal gas sensor combinations in a short optimization time. Furthermore, two gas sensors were selected, and the support vector machine (SVM) successfully distinguished between tuberculosis and healthy controls with accuracy, precision, recall, and f1-score above 98%.

articleTitle: Integrating Graph Databases into the Data Layer of Three-Tier Architecture Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Current research on database integration in enterprise systems primarily focuses on single database implementations, with limited exploration of graph database integration into existing architectures. While traditional Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS) excel in structured data management, they often struggle with complex relationship traversals in modern Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems. This research presents a systematic approach for enhanced database implementation in three-tier architecture applications, specifically addressing the challenges of managing interconnected data structures in ERP systems. The study implements parallel database configurations using MySQL for RDBMS and Neo4j for graph database, evaluating their performance through comprehensive metrics including query execution time, resource utilization, and API performance. Through extensive testing with datasets ranging from one thousand to ten million records, the experimental results demonstrate that RDBMS excels in complex analytical queries with linear scaling up to one million records, while Neo4j shows superior performance in hierarchical data traversal, maintaining consistent performance (1.7350 seconds) even at ten million records. The proposed dual database approach achieves improved system reliability, with Neo4j maintaining 100 percent success rates across all batch sizes compared to RDBMS 90 percent for larger batches, while demonstrating better resource efficiency (1.70 to 2.89 percent versus 2.70 to 3.39 percent). This research contributes to the field by introducing a Schema Complexity Index for quantifying database complexity, providing empirical evidence for optimal database selection in specific use cases, and establishing a framework for dual database integration in three-tier architectures.

articleTitle: Implementation Of Convolutional Neural Network For Cardiomegaly Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The heart plays a very important role for survival as the main organ that functions to pump blood to meet the needs of oxygen and nutrients throughout the body. However, there are several heart diseases that can cause conditions where the heart cannot perform its duties properly, including coronary artery disease, kidney disorders, hypertension, congenital abnormalities, infections, and cardiomyopathy. The result of these various heart diseases can cause cardiomegaly. Cardiomegaly occurs when the size of the heart exceeds 50% of the inner diameter of the rib cage. Cardiomegaly can be diagnosed first. Diagnosis of cardiomegaly is usually done by physical examination, blood tests, and medical imaging such as chest x-ray. Traditional diagnostic methods for heart enlargement usually involve physical examination, electrocardiogram (ECG), and medical imaging such as chest X-ray. Deep learning has emerged as the preferred method for image analysis. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is a prevalent deep learning algorithm that is specifically used in various image-related applications. This research uses DenseNet169, InceptionResNetV2, and MobileNetV2 architectures with Adagrad, Nadam, and SGD optimizers, which are evaluated using confusion matrix to determine the performance of model evaluation from each experiment. The experimental results of several models have the highest accuracy value, namely in the DenseNet169 architecture with Nadam optimizer of 90% and also the MobileNetV2 Nadam architecture reaching 87%. These two architectures can be said to be good enough to help detect cardiomegaly with image classification. This research is expected to contribute significant knowledge in the medical field as well as the development of deep learning models.

articleTitle: Smart Contract Honeytoken System using Blockchain for Internet of Things Device Security
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has introduced significant security challenges, primarily due to their limited computational resources and often inadequate built-in security mechanisms. This paper proposes a novel approach to enhancing IoT security through the implementation of a blockchain-backed honeytoken system. Leveraging Ethereum smart contracts (SCs), we present a decentralized solution that deploys and monitors honeytokens within IoT networks, triggering security measures upon detection of unauthorized access. Our implementation shows the feasibility of integrating blockchain technology with IoT security strategies, providing an additional layer of protection against potential cyber threats. The results indicate effective recognition of unauthorized access attempts, giving enhanced IoT network security. The decentralized nature of our solution ensures tamper-resistant logging and enables automated response mechanisms, significantly improving overall security posture on IoT systems. This research contributes to the body of work on IoT security using a practical, adaptable solution for IoT environments. By combining honeytoken technology with blockchain-based smart contracts, our approach addresses the security challenges posed by IoT devices using a robust framework for detecting and mitigating security breaches.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of LLM Models with RAG and Fine-Tuning T5 for Chatbot Optimization in Call Centers
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This research investigates the comparative performance of various Large Language Models (LLMs) to determine the most suitable model for XYZ Company, a call center organization aiming to integrate a chatbot solution. Chatbots significantly improve call center operations by streamlining interactions, reducing the workload on human agents, and enhancing the overall customer experience. Unlike many chatbot datasets that are document-based or contain contextual fields, the dataset of XYZ Company is composed of question-answer pairs. This unique data structure requires a customized approach to model selection. Experiments were conducted on multiple models, with RAG using Llama3 emerging as the top performer. Results indicate a BLEU score of 18%, ROUGE-1 of 46%, ROUGE-2 of 27%, ROUGE-L of 36%, BERTScore Precision of 89%, Recall of 91%, F1 of 90%, and METEOR score of 41%. These metrics underscore RAG with Llama3 to deliver accurate, efficient responses, supporting the goal of XYZ Company to implement an effective, real-world chatbot solution.

articleTitle: Evaluating K-Nearest Neighbors for X-Ray Bone Fracture Detection Using HOG, LBP, and SIFT Feature Extraction Methods
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Musculoskeletal conditions, particularly bone fractures, remain a significant global health issue, with 178 million new cases recorded annually. Accurate and efficient diagnostic tools are critical to assist clinical decisions, particularly in resource-limited settings. This study evaluates the performance of the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm for detecting bone fractures in X-ray images, employing three feature extraction methods: Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), Local Binary Patterns (LBP), and Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT). A dataset of 10,580 X-ray images, balanced across fractured and non-fractured classes, was used to train and evaluate the models across different K values (1, 3, 5, 7, 9). The results indicate that the HOG-KNN model with K=1 achieved the highest accuracy of 99.03%, outperforming LBP (98.97%) and SIFT (96.79%). These findings underscore the effectiveness of HOG in capturing structural patterns critical for fracture detection. Future research could focus on integrating advanced machine learning techniques, hybrid feature extraction methods, and larger datasets to enhance diagnostic accuracy and applicability in clinical environments.

articleTitle: RIS-Aided Ultra Dense Networks of Heterogeneous Femtocell-Macrocell Network with Clustering Method
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Ultra Dense Network (UDN) and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) are technologies useable as responses in dealing with interference problems in urban areas that have high users’ demands of coverage and capacity. This paper discusses the implementation of clustering method in addressing co-tier interference problem that occur in UDNs. The clustering method applied is an algorithm or method that groups the closest HeNBs and assigns different channels among HeNBs in the same cluster. While RIS technology helps in reducing the effects of obstructed signals between the transmitter and the receiver. Simulation experiments are conducted to evaluate the performance of the UDN according to four performance parameters that are evaluated i.e., signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR), average network energy, spectral efficiency, and bit error rate (BER). The results show that the SINR is increased applying the clustering method by 0.232dB, the result of spectral efficiency is increased by 0.08 bit/s/Hz, BER value is decreased by 0.5x10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> when number of HeNBs reaches 210. Average network energy is decreased by 4.2 J/bit. The experiment evaluates comparisons to a baseline system. It can be concluded that the use of clustering method in UDNs provides a better network and system performance compared to the baseline system.

articleTitle: Analysis Of Market Preferences For Battery Swap And Battery Charging On Electric Motorcycles Using Logit Regression
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The development of electric vehicles in Indonesia is expected to reduce emissions and support the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 2030. However, the adoption of electric vehicles remains limited due to the uneven distribution of charging infrastructure and a lack of human resources in the electric vehicle industry. This study analyzes public preferences for electric vehicle charging methods, namely Battery Swap and Battery Charging, using Garvin's dimensions as evaluation variables. Consumer preferences are crucial for the success of new technologies, as highlighted in the literature emphasizing the importance of understanding user needs and expectations. This study uses a descriptive approach to investigate the preferences of electric motorcycle users. Data was collected through questionnaires based on Garvin's eight dimensions and analyzed using validity, reliability, inferential, and logistic regression tests. The results show that Performance and Durability significantly influence user preferences. In terms of performance, the battery charging method has an odds ratio of 1.348 times greater than the battery swap, while in terms of durability, the odds ratio is 0.766 times greater. These findings indicate that battery charging offers significant advantages in performance and durability compared to battery swapping. However, this study focuses on Garvin's dimensions, such as performance and durability. It does not cover other aspects like cost, consumer psychology, or infrastructure, which the literature identifies as critical factors in adopting new technologies. The results of this study are expected to guide electric motorcycle manufacturers in enhancing battery performance and durability to meet consumer needs. Furthermore, the government is expected to accelerate the development of efficient charging infrastructure, a key practical implication of the research, to support broader and more sustainable adoption of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Exploring Tourist Perceptions of Greater Bandung Tourism Destinations: An IndoBERT-based Big Data Analytics Study on Google Maps Reviews
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The digital age has changed the way travelers seek destination information through online reviews, creating user-generated content (UGC) data that is invaluable for understanding tourist perceptions. Although previous studies have discussed destination image, most of them used questionnaire methods that tend to be biased, and the existing big data analysis is still limited to cognitive image. This study aims to analyze the cognitive and affective images of Greater Bandung tourist destinations through Google Maps reviews to identify factors that influence tourist perceptions. The research methodology involved collecting 619,113 Google Maps reviews from the top 20 tourist destinations in Greater Bandung, with data preprocessing resulting in 284,498 relevant reviews for analysis. Using the Indonesian language variant of BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), the IndoBERT model, our text classification revealed that the 'Atmosphere' dimension dominated cognitive perceptions but showed lower satisfaction compared to 'Natural attractions.' Similarly, in the affective dimensions, 'Exciting' experiences led visitor expressions yet showed lower satisfaction compared to 'Interesting' experiences. The cognitive-affective co-occurrence analysis further revealed strong connections between atmospheric elements and excitement, highlighting how physical attributes drive emotional responses. These data-driven insights enable tourism stakeholders to optimize destination management through targeted improvements in atmospheric quality while leveraging Greater Bandung's natural strengths to enhance its tourism competitiveness.

articleTitle: Exploring Youth Perspectives on Environmental Sustainability in Social Media Campaigns Using K-Means Clustering and LDA
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Indonesia is facing significant environmental challenges, including deforestation, which exacerbates climate change. To address this issues, non-governmental organizations (NGOs) have launched social media campaigns encouraging youth to adopt sustainable lifestyles. Despite the widespread awareness of environmental issues through these campaigns, there remains a disconnect between awareness and actual sustainable actions. This research investigates Indonesian youth’s perspectives on environmental sustainability campaigns by analyzing social media data. Using sentiment analysis techniques—including word embedding with IndoBERT, K-Means clustering, and Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling—the study identifies key themes in youth discourse, such as legal concerns, governance, and activism. The findings aim to provide insights into leveraging social media more effectively to bridge the gap between awareness and real-world sustainable practices.

articleTitle: Software Quality Enhancement Through Code Refactoring: An Empirical Evaluation of Roblox Game Development
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Roblox, a prominent platform in the metaverse, is recognized for its intuitive interface, robust developer support, and customizable features, making it ideal for creating virtual experiences. However, maintaining a clean and efficient code structure in game development is crucial as projects scale. Roblox Lua-based scripting environment presents challenges when managing complex codebases, particularly when critical functions are housed within a monolithic script, leading to "code smell" and lower software quality. This research focuses on addressing these challenges through code refactoring, a process that improves software quality by restructuring without altering its external behavior. The study applies various refactoring methods to a monolithic game script to enhance its software quality, using metrics such as the Number of Operations, Lack of Cohesion Metrics, Instability, Cyclomatic Complexity, Service Granularity Metrics, and Maintainability Metrics to assess improvements. The results indicate substantial improvements post-refactoring, with the NOO reduced from 17 to 5, LCOM from 0.900 to 0.556, Instability from 1.000 to 0.376, CC from 102.000 to 17.667, and MI increased from 41.897 to 84.505. These enhancements demonstrate that refactoring effectively boosts the scalability, adaptability, and quality of the game codebase, supporting its continued growth and potential expansion into additional educational subjects by maintaining a well-structured, modular codebase.

articleTitle: Feature Selection Using Ensemble Lasso Regression, Random Forest and Recursive Feature Elimination Methods in Breast Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Healthcare datasets, especially those used in cancer diagnosis, often present challenges such as high dimensionality, redundancy, and irrelevant features, which can reduce the performance and reliability of machine learning models. This research proposes a robust ensemble feature selection method to address these challenges, combining Lasso Regression, Random Forest, and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). By leveraging the complementary strengths of these algorithms, the ensemble approach aims to improve feature selection stability and enhance classification accuracy. Additionally, Shannon entropy is employed to assess data complexity and guide the feature selection process. The proposed method is applied to the Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) dataset, and its performance is evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Experimental results demonstrate that the ensemble method outperforms individual feature selection techniques, achieving higher classification accuracy and robustness in handling complex and imbalanced datasets. This study advances machine learning-based diagnostic tools by offering a reliable framework for high-dimensional medical data analysis. The findings underscore the potential of ensemble feature selection in improving interpretability, reducing computational overhead, and enhancing predictive accuracy in breast cancer diagnosis, paving the way for more effective clinical decision support systems.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Development of Electric Vehicle Adoption Intentions in North Sumatra using UTAUT Modeling
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Electric vehicle development in Indonesia is currently at an early stage of adoption, but it is projected to grow significantly in the future, especially with several government-supporting regulations. North Sumatra, one of the largest provinces with a rapidly growing economy, faces challenges in energy management and air pollution control. Electric vehicle adoption in the region could be a strategic step to support environmental sustainability and reduce the negative impact of the transportation sector on public health. This study analyzes the factors that influence the intention to adopt electric vehicles (EVs) in North Sumatra using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) model. The four main variables tested were performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social Influence, and facilitating conditions. Data was collected through an online questionnaire and an in-person survey with 295 valid respondents. Analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results show that performance expectancy and effort expectancy have a significant influence on EV adoption intention, while social influence and facilitating conditions do not show a significant influence. This study provides insights for EV developers and policymakers in promoting EV adoption in the North Sumatra region.

articleTitle: Incorporating MFCC Feature Extraction to the Classification of Respiratory Sounds by Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Respiratory diseases such as asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and lower respiratory infections are among the leading causes of death globally, particularly in remote areas. Disease diagnosis is often performed using traditional methods such as auscultation, which relies on the subjective expertise of medical professionals. As machine learning algorithms gain prominence in medical data analysis, they provide a more accurate alternative for analyzing respiratory sounds. The purpose of the research is to compare the performance of several machine learning models in classifying respiratory sounds. The method used is a machine learning-based approach utilizing Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) for feature extraction, followed by classification algorithms such as Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Naïve Bayes and Deep Neural Networks (DNN). The result of this study shows that the Random Forest classifier exhibited a superior accuracy of 79%. In contrast, SVM, DNN, and KNN classifiers demonstrated stable accuracies ranging from 75% to 77%, and Naïve Bayes recorded the lowest of 52%. Across all accuracy metrics, the Random Forest outperformed the rest of the models as the most effective choice for classifying the respiratory sound. This research provides a foundation for developing more accurate diagnostic tools for respiratory abnormality.

articleTitle: Feature-Level Early Fusion of Gabor, LBP, and HOG for Improved Diabetic Retinopathy Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is the leading cause of blindness in diabetes patients, emphasizing the need for early and accurate detection. This research explores the integration of Gabor filters, Local Binary Patterns (LBP), and Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) for feature extraction using an early fusion approach. Machine learning models, including K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), logistic regression, decision trees, and random forests, were evaluated for their ability to classify diabetic retinopathy. The experiments were conducted on the Kaggle diabetic retinopathy dataset, which consists of 700 retinal image samples. Performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and confusion matrix are used to assess the model. The Random Forest classifier achieved the best overall performance, with 72.97% accuracy. In contrast, Decision Tree showed the weakest performance, with an accuracy of 69.20%. These findings underscore the efficacy of feature-level early fusion combined with ensemble learning in improving the classification accuracy of diabetic retinopathy. This approach offers a scalable solution for clinical applications, highlighting the importance of balancing precision and recall in medical imaging tasks.

articleTitle: Integration of Item Response Theory and Fuzzy C-means in Adaptive Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Adaptive assessment has become an important tool in education to measure students’ knowledge more accurately. In the context of information and communication technology courses, traditional approaches often fail to capture the complexity and variation of students’ abilities. This article proposes the integration of Item Response Theory (IRT) with the Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) algorithm to improve the effectiveness of adaptive assessment. IRT is used to model students’ responses to test items by considering item difficulty and students’ abilities. Meanwhile, FCM is applied to group students based on their ability profiles more flexibly, accommodating uncertainty and variation in answers. This method is tested on assessment data from information and communication technology students, and compared with traditional assessment methods. The results show that the integration of IRT and FCM not only improves the accuracy of assessing students’ abilities but also provides more precise and relevant feedback. These findings demonstrate the great potential of this approach in supporting adaptive assessment that is more responsive to students’ individual needs in a dynamic educational environment.

articleTitle: ADASYN-GRU Approach for Enhanced Detection of Heavy Metals in Water Using Electrochemical Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Detecting heavy metals in water is critical for environmental monitoring. Electrochemical sensors provide a reliable solution that is easy to use, simple, fast, and cost-effective. This study presents an Adaptive Synthetic Sampling Approach for Imbalanced Learning-Gated Recurrent Unit (ADASYN-GRU) approach to improve the accuracy of heavy metal detection in water samples. The dataset consists of 606 samples distributed across three classes: Cadmium (Cd), Non-Heavy Metal, and Lead (Pb). To address class imbalance, data balancing techniques such as Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), and Adaptive Synthetic Sampling Approach for Imbalanced Learning (ADASYN) were applied. Five deep learning models, including Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Deep Neural Network (DNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), were evaluated using stratified 5-fold cross-validation. The combination of ADASYN-GRU achieved the highest performance, with an accuracy of 96.54%.

articleTitle: SmartLLM: Smart Contract Auditing using Custom Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Smart contracts, integral to decentralized finance (DeFi) and blockchain ecosystems, are increasingly vulnerable to exploits due to coding errors and complex attack vectors. Traditional static analysis tools and existing vulnerability detection methods often fail to address these challenges comprehensively, resulting in high false-positive rates and an inability to detect dynamic vulnerabilities. This paper introduces SmartLLM, a novel approach leveraging fine-tuned LLaMA 3.1 models with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of smart contract auditing. By integrating domain-specific knowledge from ERC standards and employing advanced techniques such as QLoRA for efficient fine-tuning, SmartLLM achieves superior performance compared to static analysis tools like Mythril and Slither and zero-shot LLM prompting (e.g., ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4). Experimental results demonstrate a perfect recall of 100% and an accuracy score of 70.0%, underscoring the model’s robustness in identifying vulnerabilities, including re-entrancy and access control issues. This research advances smart contract security by offering a scalable and effective auditing solution, supporting the secure adoption of decentralized applications.

articleTitle: Biopesticides Spraying System for Thrips Pest Control on Chili Plants Using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This research contributes to tackling the challenges and risk potentials during biopesticide spraying for Thrips pests on chili plants by designing and building an automation prototype of a biopesticide spraying system that performs real-time monitoring and control utilizing the Internet of Things technique. Several important parameters as determinants of spraying decisions are measured by several sensors such as the DHT22 sensor to measure temperature and humidity, an anemometer to measure wind speed, a water flow sensor to measure water flow, and a rain sensor, integrated with an ESP32 microcontroller. In addition, the IDUINO relay module 5V 2 channels ME114 is also used to control the automation function. The data that has been processed will be stored in the cloud Firebase and displayed on Android devices built using the Flutter framework. The results show that the biopesticide automation system is capable of spraying automatically according to the specified parameters, and can be controlled and monitored by the user through an Android device. Eventually, this research significantly contributes to the advancement of agricultural practices by employing current technologies to improve efficiency, safety, and sustainability, particularly in chili plant pest control.

articleTitle: Hybrid Singular Spectrum Analysis – Time Series Regression – Neural Network Model for Forecasting Inflow and Outflow Currency
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The distribution of money must be managed wisely to ensure that the amount of money circulating matches the needs of society. This research aims to obtain an accurate forecasting model for inflow and outflow in Indonesia, both at the national level and DKI Jakarta, which can capture calendar variation patterns. Neural networks (NN) are utilized to enhance forecasting accuracy as a method capable of capturing nonlinear patterns. This method is combined with Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) and Time Series Regression (TSR) into a hybrid SSA-TSR-NN. The hybrid SSA-TSR-NN method is compared to the hybrid SSA-TSR-ARIMA based on RMSE, MAPE, and MAE. SSA is employed to decompose the original time series data into trend, seasonal, and noise components. TSR is used to model trend and calendar variation components, while NN is utilized to model seasonal components and the residual of TSR noise components. This research is applied to Bank Indonesia's inflow and outflow data from July 2011 to June 2023. The conclusion drawn from the research is that, overall, SSA-TSR-NN is able to reduce the forecasting errors of SSA-TSR-ARIMA by 27%. The neurons and inputs used in NN vary for each inflow and outflow data, and a greater number of neurons does not necessarily improve the model's performance. For the forecast of the next year, the highest inflow occurs in January and April, while the highest outflow occurs in December and April.

articleTitle: Classification of Tahfidz Certification Success Among Students Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Qur'anic memorization (tahfidz) education is a vital component of the Islamic education system, with Tahfidz certification serving as a graduation requirement at Universitas Sains Al-Qur'an (UNSIQ) Wonosobo. To address inefficiencies and subjectivity in manual evaluation processes, this study applies Machine Learning algorithms to enhance evaluation accuracy and predict certification success using data from 10,969 samples, including school background, Islamic boarding school experience, BTQ scores, and academic performance. Three models XGBoost, Random Forest, and Decision Tree—were evaluated for accuracy and efficiency. XGBoost achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 92.32%, precision of 89.01%, recall of 96.25%, F1 score of 92.49%, and an AUC of 97.57%. The Decision Tree model followed closely, with an accuracy of 92.35%, precision of 89.52%, recall of 95.62%, F1 score of 92.47%, and an AUC of 96.75%. The Random Forest model also performed well, achieving an accuracy of 92.23%, precision of 88.72%, recall of 96.43%, F1 score of 92.42%, and an AUC of 97.17%. This study provides a robust, efficient, and objective framework to improve the evaluation process, ultimately enhancing tahfidz education quality.

articleTitle: The Influence of Environmental Concerns, Safety Concerns, and Health Consciousness on Organic Food Purchase Intentions in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This research investigates the factors influencing organic food purchase intentions in Indonesia, with a specific focus on consumer motivations such as environmental concerns, food safety concerns, and health consciousness. Despite growing consumer interest in organic foods and Indonesia’s significant pesticide usage, limited studies connect these elements to consumer behavior in the local context. This study fills a critical gap by examining how environmental, safety, and health concerns collectively shape attitudes toward organic foods, which in turn influence purchase intentions. By employing data modeling and visualization techniques, this research provides a comprehensive understanding of these relationships. The findings reveal that consumer attitudes play a pivotal role in shaping purchase intentions, with health consciousness emerging as the most influential factor in forming positive attitudes. These insights have significant implications for businesses, marketers, and policymakers in promoting organic food consumption. By understanding the intricate interplay between consumer motivations and purchase intentions, stakeholders can develop targeted strategies to encourage sustainable food choices and contribute to a healthier and more environmentally friendly future.

articleTitle: Multi-label Classification Aspect Analysis for Determining Term of Product Review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Product review analysis plays a vital role in understanding consumer sentiment and assessing product quality, especially laptop reviews on various aspects. Several studies on multi-aspect and multi-label have been conducted using various types of review data with transformer model, neural network, and hybrid model approaches. These approaches have shown potential in handling complex language patterns. This study aims to explore and compare the performance of five leading transformer models, namely Bidirectional Encoder Representation from Transformers (BERT), Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach (RoBERTa), Distilled BERT (DistilBERT), eXtreme Learning for Transformers Network (XLNet), and A Lite BERT (ALBERT), in multi-label aspect classification tasks. The main focus of this study is to determine the position of words containing terms in product reviews. By overcoming the limitations of traditional sentiment analysis methods that are unable to capture multiple product attributes in a single review, this study leverages the advanced feature extraction mechanism embedded in the transformer model without requiring additional manual feature engineering. This study provides a comparative analysis based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score values. The experimental results show that the ALBERT model achieves the best performance with an accuracy of 86.91%, a precision of 96.17%, a recall of 88.26%, and an F1 score of 92.05%.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of IEEE 802.11be and 802.11ax in Terms of Throughput
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: IEEE 802.11be, the seventh-generation wireless protocol, will be released soon and will perform better than IEEE 802.11ax, the sixth-generation wireless technology. The performance of competing wireless protocols at the same operating frequency—5 GHz—is reviewed in this study. We use Network Simulator (NS-3) as a simulation tool that offers flexibility, shorter setup time, and makes it easy to experiment for any scenario we need to do. Furthermore, this paper focuses on analyzing and comparing the throughput of the IEEE 802.11be (Extremely High Throughput MCS) (EhtMcs) and 802.11ax (High Efficiency MCS) (HeMcs) protocols with different client counts and specific payload sizes. Spatial flow, channel width, Guard Interval (GI), Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS), and simulation duration are among the other parameters that are set to certain values. Simulation results show that the IEEE 802.11be Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS-13) protocol has better throughput performance than the IEEE 802.11ax Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS-11) with many clients. In the simulation, the access point node is accessed from 2 to 128 clients. Simulation results show that in every situation, IEEE 802.11be performs better than IEEE 802.11ax. Wi-Fi 7 achieves up to 18 percent higher throughput for lower client counts and up to 35 percent higher throughput in scenarios with 64 to 128 clients, demonstrating its enhanced efficiency and reliability for high-density networks.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of Technological Capabilities, Open Innovation, Eco-Innovation, and Marketing Communication Capability on Corporate Performance of SMEs in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Indonesian SMEs increasingly focus on strategies to enhance corporate performance in today's highly competitive market. This study investigates the influence of Technological Capabilities, Open Innovation, Eco-Innovation, and Marketing Communication Capability on the performance of SMEs in Indonesia. The research adopts a quantitative approach, using data collected from 202 SME owners and managers across Indonesia through a structured questionnaire. The relationships between the variables were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). The results indicate that technological capabilities, eco-innovation, and marketing communication capabilities significantly and positively affect corporate performance. Furthermore, open innovation practices enable SMEs to collaborate effectively with external partners, driving product and process innovations that meet changing consumer demands. This research highlights the importance of these factors in helping SMEs improve their market position, enhance customer loyalty, and ultimately boost performance. This study offers valuable insights for SMEs seeking to improve corporate performance by leveraging technological capabilities, eco-friendly innovations, and strategic marketing communication, ensuring long-term success in the Indonesian market.

articleTitle: Exploring the Role of TAM Variables, Privacy Risk, and Trust in Social IoT Adoption
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This quantitative study examined the influence of TAM variables, perceived privacy risk, and trust on Social Internet of Things (SIoT) adoption. SIoT is an emerging technology and paradigm related to the Internet of Things (IoT), which uses social networks to facilitate social relationships between devices and individuals. This study aimed to address the problem of slow SIoT adoption because of privacy and security concerns. Research questions were developed using TAM constructs of perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and attitude, as well as the additional constructs of perceived privacy risk and trust. Data was collected from adults in the United States using IoT devices with embedded social components. Linear regression was used to determine whether there was a relationship between the independent variables of perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, perceived privacy risk, trust, and attitude toward SIoT use and the dependent variable of SIoT adoption. The result revealed a significant relationship between perceived ease of use and SIoT adoption and attitude toward SIoT use and SIoT adoption. The remaining variables of perceived usefulness, perceived privacy risk, and trust were shown to have no significant relationship with SIoT adoption. Industry practitioners and SIoT developers can use these insights as guidance when designing SIoT devices and strategies that improve adoption and enhance user experience.

articleTitle: Improving REST API Security and Software Integrity through Automated PII Detection Tool Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The increasing reliance on REST APIs for data transmission has heightened the risk of exposing Personally Identifiable Information (PII). This underscores the need for effective detection systems to safeguard privacy and comply with regulations such as GDPR and Indonesia’s Personal Data Protection Acts. This study introduces a machine learning-driven Personally Identifiable Information (PII) identification system utilizing Support Vector Machines (SVM) to examine semi-structured API responses. The system consists of two primary components: a backend module that executes PII detection and archives results in a database, and an interactive dashboard that allows users to examine, oversee, and administer detection results. The backend exhibits robust performance with elevated accuracy and precision, whereas the dashboard provides functionalities including search, severity filtering, and comprehensive result display to improve user engagement and operational decision-making. Collectively, these elements offer a comprehensive solution for enhancing REST API security and ensuring software processes comply with data privacy standards. Future endeavors will investigate real-time warning systems, sophisticated data visualization, and extensive domain modification to augment the system’s efficacy.

articleTitle: Design of Drug Sales Prediction System Using The Hybrid Demand Forecast Model
