publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Medicine plays a vital role in healthcare services, making its availability in health institutions crucial to meet public needs. Insufficient or accumulated drug supplies can decrease company profits and public trust in health institutions. To maintain the availability of drugs, health institutions need the ability to predict future drug needs obtained from drug sales data in the past. This research provides input for designing a drug sales prediction system for health institution, MS Pratama Clinic (MSPC), using a hybrid demand forecast model. This model integrates ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average) as a statistical analysis method for linear data components and LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network) for non-linear data components. This ARIMA-LSTM model was tested on drug data taken from the clinic from 2020 to 2023. Testing was carried out by measuring the MSE, RMSE, and MAPE values to ensure the most accurate model. Finally, a prototype of a drug sales prediction system that can be applied at MSPC was developed.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fraud Detection in Credit Card Transactions Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This research evaluates the effectiveness of machine learning models, including Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), and Neural Networks (NN), in detecting fraudulent credit card transactions. Fraud detection is challenging due to the highly imbalanced nature of the data, with fraudulent transactions making up only a tiny fraction of the total. To address this, RandomOverSampler balances the dataset, ensuring a fair representation of both classes. The study employs key evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC, to assess model performance comprehensively. Among the models tested, Random Forest demonstrated outstanding results, achieving 99.99 accuracy, 99.99 precision, 100 recall, 99.99 F1-score, and 100 AUC. Gradient Boosting also performed well, with 99.52 accuracy and 99.95 AUC, but RF’s perfect recall and balanced performance across all metrics make it the most reliable model. This research highlights the significance of robust models in practical fraud detection systems, ensuring precise and comprehensive transaction monitoring.

articleTitle: Edge Computing Based Terrain Detection System for SAR Robots
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Search and rescue robots are vital in disaster management. Their autonomous navigation in complex environments supports the location and assistance of victims, particularly in risky situations. It is essential that SAR robots can effectively detect terrain features that could impede or damage them. This study aims to develop a real-time terrain detection system based on edge computing, utilizing the YOLOv10n object detection model on the Raspberry Pi 4B. The YOLOv10n-based models were converted to ONNX and TFLite formats across a range of resolutions (640, 320, 256, and 160) and precision settings (FP32 and FP16 for TFLite). The models are evaluated based on several performance metrics, including latency, frames per second (FPS), power consumption, mean Average Precision (mAP), Average Precision (AP), and Average Recall (AR). The results demonstrate that ONNX models exhibit superior accuracy, with ONNX at a resolution 640 attaining a mAP of 0.925 but having low processing speed. The ONNX format model at 160 resolutions made processing speed of 23.09 FPS but having lower accuracy than ONNX model in higher resolution. The TFLite format models, despite consuming less power (5.4 W) than ONNX (7.7 W), achieve comparable accuracy with minimal losses at FP16 precision, rendering them suitable for applications where energy sensitivity is a concern. The results of this study offer valuable insights into the optimization of object detection performance on edge devices. In addition, each model highlights the inherent trade-off between accuracy, processing speed, and power efficiency.

articleTitle: Revealing Health Anxiety in Patients with Chronic Disease: A Comparison of Naïve Bayes and Decision Tree Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Chronic illnesses in Indonesia are defined as conditions with symptoms that persist for more than six months and significantly impact biological, psychological, and sociocultural functioning. These illnesses often lead to complex effects on individuals, including psychological, emotional, and psychosocial challenges. Studies suggest that the longer the duration of the illness, the more severe the emotional and psychological issues become. In light of this, the primary objective of this study is to assess anxiety levels among elderly individuals using two machine learning methods: the Naive Bayes approach and the Decision Tree method. These techniques were applied to data collected from 349 elderly residents of Semarang City, with an average age exceeding 50 years. The findings revealed that the Decision Tree method achieved an accuracy of 90%, while the Naive Bayes approach outperformed it with an accuracy of 92.37%. This represents a 2.37% improvement in accuracy and optimization using the Naive Bayes method, underscoring its effectiveness in identifying anxiety levels in older adults.

articleTitle: Analysis of Factors Influencing User Acceptance of a Car Audio Competition Management System Using a Modified UTAUT Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: In car audio competitions, "enthusiast" participants have higher dedication compared to hobbyists. These competitions help manufacturers enhance brand reputation. However, only a few organizers implement information systems in the management, marketing, and organization of competitions, even though adopting appropriate information systems can significantly improve process efficiency. A car audio competition management system can manage participant and vehicle information, competition events, and automatically calculate judging scores, enhancing efficiency and productivity. This study evaluates user acceptance of a car audio competition management system. A sample of 319 participants was obtained from questionnaires. The UTAUT framework, with the addition of the System Quality (SQ) construct from IS Success Model, was employed to understand the user acceptance of the information system. Data were analyzed using SmartPLS to assess the relationships between the constructs. The study found that SQ, Performance Expectancy (PE), and Effort Expectancy positively affect Behavioral Intention (BI), while Facilitating Condition and BI positively affect Use Behavior. Experience and voluntariness moderate various factors affecting BI and UB, with age only moderates the effect of PE factors on BI. In this use case, efforts should prioritize enhancing EE’s impact on BI and BI’s impact on UB.

articleTitle: Optimizing Machine Learning Models for Stroke Prediction Using Clinical Data and Hyperparameter Tuning Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Stroke is one of the diseases with a risk of death. It is one of the deadliest diseases and has killed many people around the world. This research aims to predict stroke disease with a machine learning approach. The dataset is obtained from the Kaggle platform with 5110 data and 12 features. The approach taken by this research focuses on aspects of clinical data to avoid geographic data bias. It compares eight machine learning models used to classify people with conditions suffering from stroke. Based on the evaluation results of all models, XGBoost is a superior model when assessed based on other evaluation metrics such as Accuracy, which reaches 91%, and AUC value of 98%. This best model will be hyperparameter tuning on the max depth parameter and obtain much better results when only using the max depth parameter with an Accuracy of 92% and an AUC value of 98%.

articleTitle: Prediction of Medicinal Leaves Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Medicinal plants are used for centuries by various cultures worldwide to treat a wide range of ailments and conditions. As there are vast numbers of medicinal plant species it will be challenging for a layman to identify them accurately. In such a situation, the experts' knowledge is sought many times. Unfortunately, lack of expertise, commercial motive and reduced availability of medicinal plants sometimes result in maltreatment due to improper plant identification. The advent of machine learning techniques and their uniqueness motivated the proposal of models that help to classify and predict medicinal plants based on their leaf images. A dataset of 30 different types of medicinal plant leaves sourced from Kaggle is used for this research. In this research a total of 19 features including the texture and shape feature of the leaves are considered extracted through image processing. Six machine learning models such as Extreme Gradient Boosting, Decision Tree, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbour, and Naïve Bayes and three ensemble models namely XGRF, XGDT and XGNB are proposed and developed using Python. XGRF achieves an AUC of 93.21% for train and test splits 80%:20% and cross-validation is employed to ensure the robustness of the model. Of the 19 features, through feature importance 8 features are observed to dominate in leaf identification. With these 8 features, XGRF is found to achieve an AUC of 93.19%. The result indicates the feasibility of the model to automatically classify medicinal leaves.

articleTitle: Mapping Web3: Analyzing Public Discourse Across Industries and Emotional Traits Using BERT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Web3 technologies—comprising decentralized finance (DeFi), non-fungible tokens (NFTs), and decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs)—spark significant public discourse, balancing enthusiasm for innovation with skepticism about associated challenges. While previous studies focus on specific Web3 domains, they often overlook the interplay between thematic discussions and emotional traits, limiting insights into adoption dynamics. This study bridges that gap using a two-stage methodology: Stage 1 categorizes Web3 discussions into industries (e.g., Core Infrastructure, DeFi, NFTs, DAOs), and Stage 2 analyzes emotional traits namely optimism, skepticism, frustration, curiosity, and concern. Annotated data from X (formerly Twitter), YouTube, and Reddit are classified using fine-tuned Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) models, achieving macro F1-scores of 0.82 for thematic and 0.84 for emotional classification. Findings reveal that curiosity and optimism dominate Core Infrastructure and Decentralized applications (DApps) discussions, while frustration is more prevalent in NFTs and DAOs. These insights provide actionable strategies for addressing barriers and amplifying drivers of Web3 adoption. Future research should explore broader demographic and temporal trends or employ advanced transformer models like the Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach (RoBERTa) and XLNet to enhance accuracy and depth.

articleTitle: Integrated Data Flow System Using Google Cloud Services in Case Study of Open Data Bus Rapid Transit Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) is an integrated bus system with high passenger capacity and frequency as an efficient alternative to congestion in urban areas. The increasing number of BRT passengers results in a surge in the volume of data processed by the system. Unfortunately, only a few cities make BRT data publicly available. In addition, the structure and format of the data vary from city to city. In this research, the author tries to simplify the process by using the method of extracting data from BRT data provider websites, transforming the data, and loading it in a centralized and more secure storage location using the Airflow data orchestration tool. Airflow is run with 2 options to analyze, namely on a virtual machine and Cloud Composer with the best comparison of convenience and cost on a virtual machine with a total of $0.05 in just one month by utilizing scheduling runs of 1 hour because the average integration process only takes one minute and system setup for 15 minutes. Compared to Cloud Composer which costs $288 per month while the Airflow process time is only used once a month due to the availability of files in the data source. In addition, Google Storage in this research is used for dirty data storage, and BigQuery for an online centralized data warehouse. Overall, this research presents an efficient and cost-effective solution for managing BRT data across cities in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Prediction of Religious Population in South Sumatra Using Interpolation on Time Series Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: Due to the rapid population growth in South Sumatra, there has been a significant concern regarding the availability of worship facilities. The gap between the number of worship facilities provided and the density of the religious population is the main problem being faced. In many cases, religious diversity is not always matched by an adequate number of worship facilities, leading to unequal access and hindering religious freedom. As a response to this problem, a comprehensive study using linear, quadratic, and cubic interpolation methods will be conducted to forecast the demand for worship facilities based on population growth trends. The related data on religious populations and worship facilities are taken from the Central Bureau of Statistics. This research shows that the Cubic interpolation method can produce the most accurate prediction for worship facility demand. Furthermore, MAPE = 0.00033213% and MSE = 2.52941176 reinforce how effective the cubic interpolation method is as the best choice. Moreover, the analysis of the ratio between religious population and worship facility capacity in 2022 also revealed a significant variation among different religions. The importance of implementing robust forecasting techniques is becoming increasingly apparent, ensuring the adequacy of worship facilities in South Sumatra's dynamic population growth.

articleTitle: Exploring Public Discourse on SDG12: Analyzing Sustainable Practices and Emotional Traits Using BERT Language Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: The growing significance of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 12 underscores the need to understand public discourse on sustainable consumption, production, and the emotional traits associated with these issues. This understanding is essential for assessing public engagement and the emotional drivers toward sustainability. This study addresses the challenge of analyzing complex textual data from digital platforms by employing a fine-tuned BERT language model for multi-label classification. The methodology involves collecting data from X and YouTube, followed by preprocessing, annotation, and fine-tuning BERT using an optimal configuration of batch size 16 and a learning rate of 2e-5. The findings demonstrate that the model achieves strong performance, with macro-average F1-scores of 0.85 classifying sustainable practices and 0.93 for identifying emotional traits such as hopefulness and frustration. The results highlight BERT's effectiveness in capturing nuanced public discourse, facilitated by robust data augmentation and balanced evaluation metrics. Future research could explore the integration of more diverse data sources along with advanced pre-trained models to improve classification accuracy and scalability. This study concludes that fine-tuned BERT models provide a reliable framework for exploring public engagement with SDG 12 and offer insights for advancing sustainable development analytics.

articleTitle: Predicting Side Effect by Using Artificial Neural Network Tuned by Camel Algorithm: Case Study Reproductive System and Breast Disorders
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study utilizes the Camel Algorithm and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to predict drug side effects that may be associated with breast and reproductive problems, based on a sample from the SIDER database. Clinical trials and post-market monitoring are popular methods for identifying adverse effects, but they frequently suffer from flaws that lead to delays or omission of important information. With systematic optimization and deep learning methods working together, predictions become more accurate. The Camel Algorithm is utilized for fine-tuning artificial neural network structures. This algorithm is famous for being very reliable. Model 2, the best ANN model on the test set, achieved an F1 score of 0.6747, precision of 0.6176, and accuracy of 0.6400. These results demonstrate that the Camel Algorithm and ANN can work together for accurate and early drug side effect predictions. This is especially true in complex cases like breast and reproduction problems. This combination would simplify the process of identifying drug side effects. Conducting further research with larger and more diverse datasets is necessary to demonstrate the applicability of the suggested method in various scenarios.

articleTitle: Social Media Marketing and Online Advertising in the Digital Landscape of ICT
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Computer Sciences, Engineering, and Technology Innovation (ICoCSETI)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the impact of digital marketing strategies, especially in the context of social media and online advertising, on consumer views of brands and their tendencies to make purchases. This study involved collecting data from 220 respondents who had received digital marketing experience through a quantitative survey method. Data processing used the SmartPLS application to identify correlations between the variables studied. It was found that marketing activities on social media platforms have a positive impact on increasing brand awareness and behavioral intention. Meanwhile, online advertising has been shown to play an important role in building consumer brand awareness and encouraging them to take the expected action. Brand awareness is useful as a mediator between the effectiveness of social media marketing, online advertising, and behavioral intention. This study provides something useful for marketers in designing more effective digital strategies to increase brand awareness and drive consumer behavioral intentions. These results are relevant for retail businesses in the competitive digital era.
